raw_title: 2027 Toyota RAV4 Woodland Gains An Inch Where It Counts, All PHEVs Get NACS And Level 3 Charging
title: 2027 Toyota RAV4 Woodland Gains An Inch Where It Counts, All PHEVs Get NACS And Level 3 Charging
raw_summary: The ever-popular Toyota RAV4 was totally redesigned for the 2026 model year, and for the first time ever it offered exclusively hybridized drivetrains . Considering how momentous that redesign was, one would expect second-year updates to be minimal, and that's mostly the case for the 2027 RAV4, but the handful of updates are good ones. The off-road-oriented RAV4 Woodland becomes slightly more off-road oriented for 2027 with a reworked suspension that adds an inch of ground clearance for a total of 9.1 inches, and all plug-in-hybrid RAV4s, including the RAV4 GR Sport , now feature an NACS port with DC fast-charging abilities and an 11-kW onboard AC charger. I'm never happy to see prices increase, but at least Toyota has kept the increases to a minimum, with different trim levels costing between $400 and $755 more than they did last year . The cheapest 2027 Toyota RAV4 you can buy is the front-wheel-drive LE trim that now costs $33,895, up $400 from last year, while the cheapest 2027 RAV4 PHEV you can buy is the all-wheel-drive SE that now costs $43,695, which is $600 dearer than last year.

The cheapest 2027 Toyota RAV4 you can buy is the front-wheel-drive LE trim that now costs $33,895, up $400 from last year, while the cheapest 2027 RAV4 PHEV you can buy is the all-wheel-drive SE that now costs $43,695, which is $600 dearer than last year.

The RAV4 Woodland's new raised suspension includes new springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers that accompany its added inch of clearance, and it also gets redesigned all-weather floor mats. That lift comes at a cost, with the 2027 Woodland being $755 more expensive at $42,250, and it gets 1 mpg worse in the city than last year — it's rated at a still outstanding 40 mpg city, 35 mpg highway, and 38 mpg combined, though. ( The Subaru Forester Wilderness Hybrid offers 0.2 inches more ground clearance than the Woodland's 9.1 inches, if that really matters to you.) The PHEV Woodland loses 3 miles of EV range, now standing at 46 miles, and though its city fuel economy dropped 3 mpg to 38, its highway mileage went up by 1 mpg to 35, and its combined rating remains 37 mpg.

The 2026 RAV4 GR Sport plug-in hybrid perplexed us because it had worse charging abilities than all other PHEV RAV4s, but that's amended for 2027. All plug-in RAV4s are now fitted with an NACS port for the first time, and the GR Sport gains DC fast-charging capability and the 11-kW onboard charger the rest of the lineup already had. Every PHEV RAV4 is now capable of charging from 10% to 80% in the same time as last year, about 35 minutes. For some reason, the 2027 RAV4 GR Sport's electric-only driving range drops by 3 miles to an estimated 45 miles of range, but that's still a good result.

Other tweaks include all the PHEVs now having their charge port on the driver's side, every model gains a standard backup camera washer, and all-wheel-drive RAV4s now have Multi-Terrain Select with Rock & Dirt mode and Mud & Sand mode. Toyota says 2027 RAV4 hybrids should hit dealer lots later this year, but PHEV models will arrive early next year.

raw_title: Would You Rather: Cadillac Escalade IQ vs. Escalade-V
title: Would You Rather: Cadillac Escalade IQ vs. Escalade-V
raw_summary: A lot of companies build EV models that have an internal-combustion analogue, with the guiding principle of, “the car you liked before, but electric.” There’s a tight thematic cohesiveness to that approach—a BMW i3 and M340i each endeavor to arrive at their optimized level of BMW 3-ness despite the differing powertrains—but the Cadillac Escalade is not like that. Yes, there are gas and electric versions, but they’re similar only inasmuch as they each avidly pursue the high-level Escalade goals of cosseting bigness and cocky braggadocio. When Tony Soprano got an Escalade in season 5 of The Sopranos , the only question around that casting decision was, what took so long? Today Tony would have more choices in his pursuit of the maximum expression of GM SUV, as do any of us with about $160,000 to spend. Namely, would you rather have a supercharged V-8 Escalade-V or an electric Escalade IQ ? Cadillac designed the Escalade-V’s exhaust to be extra boisterous , adding a 360-degree loop to the passenger’s-side pipe to equalize the length with the driver’s-side counterpart, for maximum sonic awesomeness. The IQ does not have equal-length dual exhaust. Whatever exhaust it does produce will get you into a tedious and possibly confrontational discussion of well-to-wheel emissions with your uncle at Thanksgiving. However, you’ll never have to worry about thieves stealing your catalytic converters, so I’ll call that one a draw.

However, you’ll never have to worry about thieves stealing your catalytic converters, so I’ll call that one a draw.

Looking at the specs, I’m surprised to see that the Escalade-V weighs eight pounds more than the IQ. Hold on, that doesn’t sound right—let me check my notes—sorry, my curb-weight figure for the Escalade-V inadvertently included a Toyota GR86 parked on its roof. Remove that extra car, and the supercharged Escalade is quite a bit lighter: 6290 pounds for the V, and a pavement-crushing 9120 pounds for the IQ.

Despite the weight disparity, the two Slades are evenly matched in a drag race, with the 750-hp IQ trailing the 682-hp V by a couple tenths of a second to 60 mph (4.5 seconds to 4.3). On a rolling start from 5 mph, they’re tied at 4.7 seconds, and passing a dawdler will be a quicker task in the IQ: 50 to 70 mph in 2.6 seconds, versus 3.1 seconds for the loud Caddy.

Now, I’m old enough to remember the days when a Ferrari 458 Italia felt like it had pretty decent passing power, but the Escalade IQ’s 2.1-second 30-to-50-mph time beats the Ferrari by a tenth. If the IQ had been part of our Chariots of the Gods comparison test in 2011, its 50-to-70-mph time would have slotted it a tenth of a second behind the 458 and two-tenths ahead of the McLaren MP4-12C. Neither of those, when accelerating, heave their hoods skyward like a 70-foot Viking sportfish climbing on a plane, but the Escalade IQ certainly does. And they say EVs don’t bring any drama to the experience—behind the wheel, the IQ accelerating like my favorite Ferrari of all time feels as improbable as it actually is, like the vehicle itself is struggling to cope with its superpowers. An Escalade-V drives more like a mutant CT5-V Blackwing, and it’s definitely the Escalade where the driver’s seat is more desirable than one of the chauffeur chairs in back.

If we accept that one of the primary goals for an Escalade is to project brash confidence, and that hugeness is fundamental to that project, the Escalade IQ wins going away. It reminds me of a scaled-up Rolls-Royce Cullinan in the side profile, and there’s a lot of side to behold: the IQ is more than a foot longer than the gas-powered Escalade. It’s also just newer, and I think it helps the premium aura not to have a bunch of Chevys and GMCs out there copping your style with very similar bodies. Also: rear-axle steering is unequivocally a flex, and the internal-combustion Escalade doesn’t have it.

Inside, both Escalades offer huge screens, lots of leather, and power-operated doors. However, only the IQ is eligible for the Curated by Cadillac program, wherein buyers fork over an additional $54,995 and get to choose from a huge palette of colors, inside and out. With 44 interior color choices, you can certainly spec a one-of-one IQ, while the Escalade-V sticks with “Yukon Denali, but fancier” as a guiding principle. Advantage, IQ.

When we’re discussing EVs versus internal combustion, range is usually an easy win for the gas-powered candidate. But not here—the Escalade-V has an EPA-rated 312 miles of range, while the IQ gets a 465-mile rating. Yes, the V will refuel a lot quicker, but you’ll be stopping way more often. And if your gas pump stops at $100, you might technically need to fill twice to top off the 24-gallon tank with premium.

title: New ID. AURA is the mainstream EV VW needs
raw_summary: Volkswagen built its global empire on the promise of affordable, accessible transportation, embodied by the iconic Type 1 Beetle. Now facing an existential crisis after a decades-long push upmarket , the automaker faces a reckoning – and a retreat back into affordable, mass-market electric sedans like the new FAW-VW ID. As the Model 3 approaches its 11th year in public view, the recently revealed all-electric ID. AURA L5 and VW JETTA looks like it could be a compelling rival to the mainstream M3.

Like the Ford Model T, the original VW Type 1 Beetle was an engineering-led answer to a basic problem: making family transportation affordable and accessible to the masses. And regardless of how you feel about Elon Musk, the Tesla Model 3 has become the spiritual successor to those cars, bringing electric transportation to millions of mainstream drivers. As the Model 3 approaches its 11th year in public view, the recently revealed all-electric ID. AURA L5 and VW JETTA looks like it could be a compelling rival to the mainstream M3.

Co-developed by Volkswagen’s Chinese and German design teams and set to be built by the FAW-VW JV , the ID. AURA L5 is an Accord/Camry-sized electric family car a practical fastback-style rear hatch, frameless doors, and a claimed “84.4% usable floor-area ratio.” The power-operated hatchback opens its maw more than 70 degrees, revealing a 39″ wide opening that can handle groceries, luggage, golf clubs, pets, bodies – whatever you got.
Don’t take my word for it, though. This is the original text from the company’s press release (translated from Chinese by Google):

The ID. AURA L5 is a pure electric family sedan, jointly designed by Chinese and German design teams, and highly replicates the design essence of the ID. AURA concept car shown at the 2025 Shanghai Auto Show. Its short overhang and long wheelbase proportions create a sleek and flowing coupe-like stance, achieving a “usable floor area ratio” of 84.4%. The sides feature true frameless doors, semi-concealed door handles, and an electric hatchback tailgate with an opening angle exceeding 70°, and an opening width exceeding 1000 mm, greatly improving the convenience of loading and unloading large items, deeply integrating fastback aesthetics with practicality. Some models will be equipped with LiDAR and feature the Hyper Sense 8 end-to-end large model, making daily travel easier and more convenient for customers.

The production version of the ID. AURA L5 is expected to pack the same 155 kW (~208 hp) electric motors announced when the concept AURA L5 was first shown last year (battery specs were not released), and was shown as part of a broader product announcement of what VW Group China would be showcasing at this year’s China International Import Expo (CIIE). These include the first two models fully equipped with Volkswagen Group’s locally developed VEGA “integrated technology matrix” (read: software), and the Volkswagen Anhui intelligent pure electric “coupe” crossover.

The announcement coincides with reports from outlets like Autocar and Reuters that Volkswagen is evaluating whether to deploy its China-developed electrical architecture across the majority of its European markets.

“According to internal discussions confirmed by Group board member and Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer,” reports Autocar’s Greg Kable, “up to 75% of the firm’s core models in Europe could eventually use the China Electronic Architecture.”

raw_title: Marini out as Qatar grid is reduced to 16 riders
title: Marini out as Qatar grid is reduced to 16 riders
raw_summary: Honda MotoGP rider Luca Marini has withdrawn from the main Qatar Grand Prix race, reducing the field to 16 participants. Twenty-two full-time riders are entered in the series - but Yamaha is absent in full from the Qatar weekend due to the geopolitical situation, and Pecco Bagnaia was ruled out of the weekend after fracturing his foot in the sprint. Bagnaia will undergo surgery on a pair of metatarsal fractures in his right foot on Monday or Tuesday. Now, Marini has withdrawn from the weekend, too, as he has continued to struggle with fatigue after a viral infection last month. He was able to compete last weekend at Sepang but has laboured from the get-go here, finishing a low-key 13th in the sprint before pulling out following the warm-up. There are questions, too, about whether Maverick Vinales will take the start for Tech3 KTM. A despondent Vinales, who is still not fit after his shoulder injury last year, said he "doesn't want anymore to ride like this". But he did run in the warm-up, and there has been no communication from Tech3 about him sitting out the race. If the grid size ends up at 16, it means Jorge Martin would need to beat just one rider to take the championship fight to Portugal - even if Marc Marquez were to win the grand prix.

raw_title: This Is The Only Road In The US That Closes For Snakes
title: This Is The Only Road In The US That Closes For Snakes
raw_summary: Street takeovers are a menace. Heck, the disruptive crime has jurisdictions like Compton installing new medians to prevent takeovers. This, however, isn't that kind of takeover. Twice a year, thousands of snakes take over a small road in Illinois. It's the sort of thing that would be enough to make Indiana Jones ditch his motorcycle, drop his whip, and head for the hills. Now, before you conjure mental images of "Raiders of the Lost Ark" and a writhing tangle of venomous vipers, this is all part of nature. Though there are still thousands of slithery critters on the so-called "Snake Road," a few of which are venomous. It's enough to shut down the road that runs through part of the Shawnee National Forest in southern Illinois. Every year, the little road closes to vehicle traffic due to the influx of scaly travelers. Not once, but twice every trip around the sun. In fact, it's the only known road in the United States to shut down in observance of a reptile migration. The shutdown isn't meant to protect the national forest's human visitors, either – it's to make sure the road-going snakes can complete their journey unharmed.

Twice a year, thousands of snakes take over a small road in Illinois. It's the sort of thing that would be enough to make Indiana Jones ditch his motorcycle, drop his whip, and head for the hills. Now, before you conjure mental images of "Raiders of the Lost Ark" and a writhing tangle of venomous vipers, this is all part of nature. Though there are still thousands of slithery critters on the so-called "Snake Road," a few of which are venomous.

It's enough to shut down the road that runs through part of the Shawnee National Forest in southern Illinois. Every year, the little road closes to vehicle traffic due to the influx of scaly travelers. Not once, but twice every trip around the sun. In fact, it's the only known road in the United States to shut down in observance of a reptile migration. The shutdown isn't meant to protect the national forest's human visitors, either – it's to make sure the road-going snakes can complete their journey unharmed.

Shawnee National Forest is a biodiverse landscape spanning 289,000 acres between the Mississippi River and the Ohio River. It's home to around 35 migratory species of snakes and 23 species of migrating amphibians. Twice a year, those critters make the trek between the national forest's limestone bluffs and the LaRue Swamp. In the spring, the reptiles and amphibians travel from the bluffs to the swamp. In the fall, the ectothermic excursionists do the trip in reverse order, returning to the bluffs from the LaRue Swamp. Be it a slither, crawl, or hop, these reptiles and amphibians are on a mission.

The adventure takes the animals right across Forest Service Road 345, also known as LaRue Road. "We call it Snake Road," Forest Service Enforcement Officer Anderson Harris told CBS Evening News . It's a fitting name, too. The Forest Service closes the road because of snake, reptile, and amphibian migrations from March 15 to May 15 and September 1 to October 30 every year. "That protects animals from being incidentally killed by vehicles running over them," Officer Harris added. "It's the only road in the U.S., to my knowledge, that we close for migrations of the amphibians and reptiles."

At first, locals weren't so pleased with the idea of closing the road for four months of the year. Some of the more cruel motorists made a game of killing as many snakes as they could on the road. Eventually, they came around to the idea of closing the road. Best to leave the reptilian travelers in peace, even if you're curious.

Before you ask, yes, you can go check out the cold-blooded crossers for yourself. While the road is closed to cars, it's open to visitors on foot. That said, you might want to pay close attention to where you step. Of the snakes that migrate through Shawnee National Forest's Snake Road, at least three are venomous. For starters, there's the timber rattlesnake, a pit viper with a maraca for a tail. There's also the cottonmouth, also known as the water moccasin. Finally, the eastern copperhead, which can average up to three feet in length.

Again, you might want to steer clear of Snake Road if you have a bad case of ophidiophobia. If herpetoculture is your hobby of choice, it might be worth checking out. That said, collecting the snakes as they cross the road is against the law. Of course, if you're looking for something viper-esque, a clean Ram SRT-10 might be a charming enough snake. Frankly, you'd probably rather a series of snakes choose to shut down a little service road in Illinois than find a giant snake nestled in your engine bay. That is, unless Steve Irwin is your kindred spirit or something. If you're more like Indiana Jones, you'd be more likely to curse, "Why did it have to be snakes?"

raw_title: Can Leaving A Car Battery On Concrete Actually Damage It?
title: Can Leaving A Car Battery On Concrete Actually Damage It?
raw_summary: If you're into cars, and particularly driving and wrenching on older cars , you'll have doubtless come across old wives' tales about driving and running them. Examples include older vehicles being safer, even though they lack modern safety equipment like airbags, because they're made of thicker steel. Or that filling up with high octane fuel will boost the horsepower of even the most ordinary engine. Both are generally untrue, but what about the one that says leaving a car battery on concrete can damage it? Like those other two examples, the battery myth is just that. You won't hurt a battery by leaving it on a concrete floor. But also like the safety and octane stories, there's a grain of truth to it. Modern cars are designed to crumple to absorb impacts, and that can make them look less safe after a relatively small accident. And some performance cars, or tuned cars, do deliver more output with higher octane fuel. Which is why, by the same token, even today, you might hear the concrete floor battery warnings repeated by folks who have more experience in looking after cars than you do.

Examples include older vehicles being safer, even though they lack modern safety equipment like airbags, because they're made of thicker steel.
article_paragraphs: If you're into cars, and particularly driving and wrenching on older cars , you'll have doubtless come across old wives' tales about driving and running them. Examples include older vehicles being safer, even though they lack modern safety equipment like airbags, because they're made of thicker steel. Or that filling up with high octane fuel will boost the horsepower of even the most ordinary engine. Both are generally untrue, but what about the one that says leaving a car battery on concrete can damage it?

Like those other two examples, the battery myth is just that. You won't hurt a battery by leaving it on a concrete floor. But also like the safety and octane stories, there's a grain of truth to it. Modern cars are designed to crumple to absorb impacts, and that can make them look less safe after a relatively small accident. And some performance cars, or tuned cars, do deliver more output with higher octane fuel. Which is why, by the same token, even today, you might hear the concrete floor battery warnings repeated by folks who have more experience in looking after cars than you do.

Cars have changed a lot in the last 70 years , but their 12-volt batteries — with the exception of lightweight packs like the lithium-ion unit in the Porsche 911 GT3 — look mostly the same. They're still heavy, 12-volt lead-acid batteries, they're still encased with tough, injection-molded plastic, and can still be charged without unhooking the terminals.

But before then, batteries looked quite different, and this is partly responsible for the concrete floor myth. Early car batteries, which put out just 6 volts, were usually encased in wooden boxes, often containing a glass jar full of acid. In the 1920s, battery makers switched to hard rubber cases, which resisted corrosion from the acid inside, and were more durable than glass. But over time they could crack and split due to heat and vibration, and if these batteries were placed on the ground, yes, they could discharge.

That's not a problem with modern plastic cases, which are far more durable, though it's worth remembering that any battery will naturally discharge over time, no matter what the outer case is made from. And that's possibly another source of the concrete myth. How quickly it loses its charge can depend heavily on the temperature of the area its stored. A battery stored in a cold environment will hang on to its charge longer than one stored in a hot space.

Now you know that storing a battery on your concrete garage floor won't do it any harm, despite what your grandpa told you. But the reverse is definitely not true. Spilling the contents of a car battery on concrete can do the floor real damage. Some modern batteries use Absorbent Glass Mat (AGM) technology, making them effectively spill proof. But many still consist of traditional flooded wet cells that can spill when tipped. The electrolyte solution inside includes a large amount of sulfuric acid.

Concrete, on the other hand, contains alkaline calcium compounds, and when the two meet, they react, eating away at the surface of the concrete floor. If left, the acid can cause pitting, staining, small craters and a chalky, dusty surface. And once the top coating is eaten away, the floor is more susceptible to absorbing future spills and moisture. Flooring experts recommend spills be cleaned up right away, but not just with water, because that can spread the acid. Instead, create an alkaline paste using water and baking soda, leave it to fizz on the floor surface, then scrub gently, and rinse with water. And don't forget your PPE.

Koenig Specials GmbH was founded by eccentric millionaire and successful racing driver Willy König (sometimes spelled “Willy Koenig”) in 1977 to formally sell kits and parts that Koenig had been developing and selling since 1974.
Here we see Willy König (right) with his son, in front of three of his creations. Image courtesy of Koenig Specials GmbH.

The cars built by Willy and his team were extreme to say the least, so extreme that former friend Enzo Ferrari demanded that any Ferrari modified by Koenig have its badges removed or face legal action – as the company no longer considered it to be a Ferrari.

Love them or hate them, Willy and the team at Koenig had a significant influence on the global car tuning and modification scene. The company sold wide body kits, suspension systems, performance engine parts and they offered fully-built cars.

One of the company’s most famous creations was an extensively modified Ferrari Testarossa with an avant garde body kit and a significantly modified twin-turbo engine capable of 1,000+ bhp. They also built a Porsche 911 Turbo with up to 550 bhp and a top speed not far off 200 mph.

A slew of wild cars rolled out of the Koenig facilities during the 1970s and 1980s, today they’re considered quite collectible but only to a specific kind of collector – one who cares more for the cars’ unusual nature than their lost originality.

raw_title: When The Speed Limit Changes, Do You Slow Down Before Or After The Road Sign?
title: When The Speed Limit Changes, Do You Slow Down Before Or After The Road Sign?
raw_summary: The rules surrounding speed limit signs are standard across the country, but how they're followed can vary. The rules, however, are fairly clear. The federal government doesn't set speed limits, even on interstates. Instead, states and local municipalities depend on traffic engineers to help decide posted speed limits. Those are determined by considering laws, the areas where the speed limit will be posted, and the safety of the area, including the flow of traffic and frequency of accidents. (Not, though, the long-touted "85th-percentile rule." ) Traffic engineers often refer to their bible, the 1,100-page-plus Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices , written and revised by the Federal Highway Administration. If you're curious, turn to Page 84 of the revised 11th edition, where the section "Speed Limit Signs and Plaques" resides. The item to pay attention to is number 14: "Speed Limit (R2-1) signs, indicating speed limits for which posting is required by law, shall be located at points of change from one speed limit to another."

article_paragraphs: The rules surrounding speed limit signs are standard across the country, but how they're followed can vary. The rules, however, are fairly clear. The federal government doesn't set speed limits, even on interstates. Instead, states and local municipalities depend on traffic engineers to help decide posted speed limits. Those are determined by considering laws, the areas where the speed limit will be posted, and the safety of the area, including the flow of traffic and frequency of accidents. (Not, though, the long-touted "85th-percentile rule." )

Traffic engineers often refer to their bible, the 1,100-page-plus Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices , written and revised by the Federal Highway Administration. If you're curious, turn to Page 84 of the revised 11th edition, where the section "Speed Limit Signs and Plaques" resides. The item to pay attention to is number 14: "Speed Limit (R2-1) signs, indicating speed limits for which posting is required by law, shall be located at points of change from one speed limit to another."

To bluntly translate this government literature: The speed limit starts at the sign. That means drivers should be slowing down while approaching a slower speed zone, arriving at the correct speed when crossing next to it. If the speed limit sign is higher, the driver should not accelerate until reaching the posted sign. Those of you who see that 55 mph sign on a highway that eventually turns into a 70 mph expressway know better, but you still speed up knowing in less than a quarter-mile, your speed will be fine. Legally, though, it's not ... not just yet.

State officers agree. The Colorado State Patrol, after polling the same question on Facebook , referred followers to the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control devices as well. California Highway Patrol Officer Dan Olivas informed a reader inquiring on this same question in Anaheim's Daily Bulletin that the state Department of Transportation's literature "refers to placing speed limit signs at the start of the designated speed zone, which alludes to the speed limit zone starting where the sign is placed."

raw_title: What's got F1 drivers so worried about Brazilian GP spectacle
title: What's got F1 drivers so worried about Brazilian GP spectacle
raw_summary: The Brazilian Grand Prix has been witness to many famous charges from the lower reaches of the Formula 1 grid because overtaking has historically been easy. But there are genuine fears among F1 drivers that the peculiarities of the 2026 regulations will neuter the spectacle at Interlagos on Sunday afternoon.
summary: The Brazilian Grand Prix has been witness to many famous charges from the lower reaches of the Formula 1 grid because overtaking has historically been easy. But there are genuine fears among F1 drivers that the peculiarities of the 2026 regulations will neuter the spectacle at Interlagos on Sunday afternoon.
article_paragraphs: The Brazilian Grand Prix has been witness to many famous charges from the lower reaches of the Formula 1 grid because overtaking has historically been easy.
But there are genuine fears among F1 drivers that the peculiarities of the 2026 regulations will neuter the spectacle at Interlagos on Sunday afternoon.

Only one week ago in Mexico, Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris were both bemoaning the energy deployment ramp-down rates that kick in once F1 cars clear a certain threshold of speed. Hamilton called them "stupid" and Norris said they "kind of ruin racing".

And the 2026 rules are why drivers including Hamilton and Max Verstappen, who have both tasted success in Brazil when starting from lowly grid positions, feel their chances of coming through the field are much reduced.

Hamilton, who will start 20th after picking up a 10-place grid penalty, suggested "overtaking will be very, very, very hard. I'm not sure you're going to see the same sort of races that you've seen in the past".

Hamilton himself won the 2021 Brazilian GP from 10th on the grid, having come from the very back in the sprint race with a new engine fitted, but he feels the fact every car will shed drag in straight mode, rather than being offset like they were racing under the old DRS rules, means the 2026 race is likely to be more static.
This reading of the situation was echoed by Verstappen, who won the 2024 edition of this race from 17th on the grid.
"Now we don't have DRS anymore and the overtake mode is very limiting around here because of the long straight, everyone is draining the battery," he said.

title: Aston Martin Once Built A DB10 That Never Went To Production
raw_summary: If you look at the lineage of Aston Martin's main production grand tourer over the years, it goes straight from the DB9 of the 2000s and early 2010s to the DB11 in 2016. Why did they seemingly just skip DB10? Is the number 10 unlucky in British culture? Turns out, A) it didn't and B) no. In fact, Aston Martin did indeed build a DB10; it just never made production. A few years before the DB11 came along, work was underway on Daniel Craig's fourth James Bond movie, "Spectre." Director Sam Mendes, who helmed the wildly successful and, by most accounts, very good "Skyfall," was returning, and he wanted a new Aston Martin for Bond to drive. Enter the DB10, a car that was originally a concept sketch for the next Vantage , but became its own special model brought to life specifically for the movie. Fun fact: this was apparently the very first time an entirely new car was made for a Bond film.
summary: If you look at the lineage of Aston Martin's main production grand tourer over the years, it goes straight from the DB9 of the 2000s and early 2010s to the DB11 in 2016. Why did they seemingly just skip DB10? Is the number 10 unlucky in British culture?
article_paragraphs: If you look at the lineage of Aston Martin's main production grand tourer over the years, it goes straight from the DB9 of the 2000s and early 2010s to the DB11 in 2016. Why did they seemingly just skip DB10? Is the number 10 unlucky in British culture? Turns out, A) it didn't and B) no. In fact, Aston Martin did indeed build a DB10; it just never made production.

A few years before the DB11 came along, work was underway on Daniel Craig's fourth James Bond movie, "Spectre." Director Sam Mendes, who helmed the wildly successful and, by most accounts, very good "Skyfall," was returning, and he wanted a new Aston Martin for Bond to drive. Enter the DB10, a car that was originally a concept sketch for the next Vantage , but became its own special model brought to life specifically for the movie. Fun fact: this was apparently the very first time an entirely new car was made for a Bond film.

Mendes wanted the car to serve as a sort of spiritual successor — but not a direct retro-adaptation of — the superspy's iconic DB5. Aston design boss Marek Reichman spoke to Top Gear about it at the time, saying, "This isn't a mere pastiche of the original," and that "We don't want a parody, otherwise why not just get an original DB5."

To modern eyes, the DB10 may look like a lot of the Astons that have come since, but at the time, it was quite a departure. It was built using the underpinnings of the V8 Vantage of the era, and eventually fulfilled its original purpose, heavily influencing the next-gen Vantage that showed up in 2018. A shark-like front end would eventually be seen on the production DB11, and behind that gaping maw sat a 4.7-liter V8. It had a longer wheelbase than the Vantage it was built upon while being almost as wide as the One-77 hypercar .

Within movie canon, Q says the DB10 can go from zero to 60 mph in 3.2 seconds. The car was also fully bulletproof, according to Q, and hiding "a few tricks up her sleeve," such as an ejector seat with a parachute system, a rear-mounted twin-barrel machine gun with a rear window digital targeting system, and two flamethrowers in the exhaust.

In reality, the Aston had a claimed a zero-to-60 time of 4.7 seconds and a top speed of 190 mph. All of the DB10's body panels were made of carbon fiber, and only 10 were ever built — eight used in filming, two for promotional purposes. The promo cars probably didn't shoot flames.

As cool and undoubtedly pretty as the DB10 itself is, its big car chase in "Spectre" is a bit of an odd one to watch. Bond is being pursued through the streets of Rome by Dave Bautista in an even crazier-looking British sports car that also never made production, the Jaguar C-X75. The sequence is awkwardly shot like a car commercial, and it doesn't feel like they're going very fast.

In fact, they're driving so leisurely that Bond still has the bandwidth to hop on a whole phone call with Moneypenny for a bit of exposition. That said, I'm a car reviewer, not a movie critic, but here's the scene in question so you can judge for yourself.

title: India-bound Toyota Land Cruiser FJ Likely To Get A Diesel Engine
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Lack of a diesel engine is one of the main gripes about Toyota’s new global C-segment rugged SUV The India-bound Toyota Land Cruiser FJ ticks nearly all the main boxes for a rugged SUV, but performance is one of its main downsides. More than the sheer lack of power, purists particularly miss the availability of a diesel engine option. A company official has hinted that a fix may be in the works. For the uninitiated, the Toyota Land Cruiser FJ is a body-on-frame C-segment SUV that slots below the Toyota Fortuner. Most customers prefer diesel engines in such vehicles for their strong pulling power at low engine speeds and higher fuel economy. In a recent interview with Cars.co.za, Andrew Kirby, the President and CEO of Toyota’s South African subsidiary, said that “there’s a good likelihood” for the introduction of a diesel engine for the Land Cruiser FJ. However, Kirby indicated that, at least in South Africa, the potential diesel engine is a few years away. He did admit that a diesel engine would “make a big difference to the performance” of the Land Cruiser FJ. Currently, Toyota offers the FJ Cruiser only with the 2TR-FE 2.7-litre naturally aspirated four-cylinder petrol engine globally, along with a 6-speed automatic transmission and a part-time 4WD system. Also Read: Toyota Innova Hycross & Hyryder Hybrids Set New Records For Elevation Gains On-road performance of the currently available configuration has been widely criticised in key markets, including South Africa and Australia. For reference, Toyota has tuned the 2TR-FE engine in the Land Cruiser FJ to deliver 122 kW (164 hp) at 5,200 rpm and 245 Nm of torque at 4,000 rpm. In India, rumour has it Toyota Kirloskar Motor (TKM) plans to offer the Land Cruiser FJ in petrol, petrol-electric hybrid, and petrol-electric plug-in hybrid variants. The petrol variant should have the 2TR-FE engine under the hood, and the electrified variants may use a modified version of the same. A diesel engine, if introduced globally, could be added at some point. Also Read: Toyota Innova Crysta Limo Launched In India At Rs. 19.95 Lakh As with every non-Maruti Suzuki-derived Toyota sold in our market, the Land Cruiser FJ could be way costlier than other models in its segment, with prices starting at around Rs. 30 lakh (ex-showroom) in the base configuration. TKM will manufacture the Land Cruiser FJ in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra. The company is likely to launch it sometime in 2028.

title: Everyone wants an electric pickup truck. I want more electric 125cc motorcycles
raw_summary: If you follow the EV industry in North America, you’d be forgiven for thinking that the future of transportation revolves around electric SUVs and pickups. Every week seems to bring another teaser from a startup promising to reinvent the family car or truck. The latest electric SUVs, “coming soon” tiny trucks, lifestyle trucks, modular trucks, etc. Companies like Slate, TELO, and countless others have generated plenty of excitement, even if many of them still have everything left to prove. Don’t get me wrong – I hope they succeed. We need more affordable electric vehicles. But after spending nearly two decades covering a specific part of the electric-vehicle space and a good chunk of that time traveling around the world to see how people actually get around, I can’t help but wonder if we’re chasing the wrong prize here.

The latest electric SUVs, “coming soon” tiny trucks, lifestyle trucks, modular trucks, etc. Companies like Slate, TELO, and countless others have generated plenty of excitement, even if many of them still have everything left to prove.

Don’t get me wrong – I hope they succeed. We need more affordable electric vehicles. But after spending nearly two decades covering a specific part of the electric-vehicle space and a good chunk of that time traveling around the world to see how people actually get around, I can’t help but wonder if we’re chasing the wrong prize here.
Because while the West keeps trying to electrify pickup trucks and SUVs, much of the world has already settled on a far more sensible transportation appliance.
Western readers often think of a sedan as the world’s “normal” or “sensible” vehicle.
But go traveling almost anywhere in Asia, and that illusion disappears in about five minutes.

The roads are filled with Honda Clicks and CG125s, Hero Splendors, Yamaha NMAXs and YBR125s, and countless other small-displacement motorcycles. They carry workers to jobs, students to school, families to dinner, and every imaginable cargo in between.

They’re the delivery vans. They’re the commuter cars. They’re grocery getters, family transportation, and work trucks. And perhaps more importantly, they transport hundreds of millions of people every single day.

You don’t have to spend long in places like the Philippines before realizing something else: these aren’t really “motorcycle cultures.” They’re just transportation cultures. People ride these machines because they make sense.

raw_summary: Formula 1 might have proved in Brazilian Grand Prix qualifying that its 2026 cars can run on full wet tyres, but its problems in handling rainy conditions are not over yet. In fact, Mercedes driver George Russell warned that if the kind of weather that drivers faced on Saturday is repeated in the race, then the chances of trouble are very high.

article_paragraphs: Formula 1 might have proved in Brazilian Grand Prix qualifying that its 2026 cars can run on full wet tyres, but its problems in handling rainy conditions are not over yet.
In fact, Mercedes driver George Russell warned that if the kind of weather that drivers faced on Saturday is repeated in the race, then the chances of trouble are very high.

"I love driving in the rain here but, at some point, if that was a race, there was no way we should be driving in that because the chances of seeing a really, really horrific incident are very, very high," he said.

One of the running themes throughout the start of the current rules era was that the high-torque characteristics of the current power units allied to the performance of Pirelli's intermediates were a total mismatch.
Drivers had warned that problems in getting temperature into the inters - which were the default wet-weather tyre - made them quite a challenge.

Alpine's Pierre Gasly, who was far from impressed after running a wet-weather tyre test at Magny-Cours after the Miami GP in May, predicted an "elimination game" when talk of them needing to be raced earlier in the year cropped up.
Recent races have proven that the inter was not as bad as initially feared, but the doubts about the wet remained until now.
F1 has faced years where it has been heavily restricted in terms of how wet things got before sessions could not run.

article_paragraphs: As has been widely reported, Tesla is about to end Cybertruck production. The Cybertruck has been a shocking failure. I’m sure there are more detailed analyses out there somewhere, but this short response on X from Ben McCombe that Tina Casey included in her article on the matter sums it up very well:

That’s pretty wild. A net project loss of around $2 billion. Now, I have to admit that I haven’t fact checked the numbers here, but what we know for certain is that Tesla planned to produce a lot of Cybertrucks per year and ended up producing a small fraction of that target. In fact, the annual sales target for the Cybertruck was higher than 125,000 — it was 250,000, with a goal of getting up to 500,000!

The Cybertruck was hyped up as having more reservations than any vehicle in history and was supposedly going to shatter records and transform the market. I warned people on many occasions that the reservation total was not a real reservation total and was definitely not a reliable indicator of demand because a) a reservation only required a $100 refundable deposit, and b) a ton of people made reservations after Elon Musk said that you could lock in the price of lifetime Full Self Driving when making a reservation (so, you’d only have to pay $6,000 for FSD no matter how much the cost of it went up in the following years). Anyway, the Cybertruck had other issues as well when it finally arrived. It cost about twice as much as it was supposed to cost and it had about half as much range as it was supposed to have. In other words, it was not even close to the vehicle it was supposed to be — its range per dollar cost was about ¼ what it was supposed to be.

The Cybertruck was supposed to be the next big thing after the Tesla Model Y. It was supposed to disrupt the gigantic US pickup truck market. The Model S was a superb and widely acclaimed car, if a bit more expensive than the mass market could afford. The Model S did in fact compete superbly well with the leaders in its segment, the BMW 7 Series and Mercedes S-Class. The Tesla Model X brought a similar offering in a larger package with some fun extra elements (falcon-wing doors, self-presenting doors, a third row). The Tesla Model 3 then completely shook the automotive world as a tremendous market phenomenon and perhaps the biggest product launch in history (in terms of total revenue). The Tesla Model Y was basically the Model 3 in a more popular crossover package and eventually became a much higher selling vehicle. In fact, it became the highest selling vehicle model of any kind in multiple years. Then JB Straubel stepped down as CTO.

Due to their EV passions, JB Straubel and Elon Musk were introduced to each other and had lunch together to talk about electric airplanes (Elon’s dream) and then electric cars (because JB talked more sense into Elon). Then the two of them were introduced to Marc Tarpenning and Martin Eberhard, who had founded Tesla Motors and just barely got started on the idea. After a while, Tarpenning and Eberhard left the company, and Musk and Straubel truly led its development and growth into an automotive superpower (as briefly described above). Since JB Straubel stepped down from his role as CTO of Tesla, however, if one thinks about it, it’s hard to identify any successful product launch from the company or much significant improvement at all.

Straubel left his CTO position in July 2019. The Model Y was unveiled in March 2019 and was about ⅔ the same as the Model 3. It would seem that getting the Model Y designed and prepared for launch was the last big project Straubel worked on. (Note that the Semi was unveiled in November 2017 but was long delayed due to battery supply, according to Elon Musk.) Since the Model Y, what significant product launch have we seen from Tesla? There was the Cybertruck, as we’ve already discussed. That was unveiled in November 2019. When you think about the timing now, did Straubel disagree strongly with Musk on the Cybertruck and decide it was time to move on when Musk pushed forward with his idea for an electric truck? It took another 4+ years for Tesla to start delivering the Cybertruck, in contrast to Model Y deliveries starting in January 2020, less than a year after the model was unveiled. More recently, the Cybercab has been developed, unveiled, and is now in production. A consumer car smaller and cheaper than the Model 3 was never developed and unveiled — just a stripped down, decontented Model 3 — and there basically haven’t been any other product unveilings since Straubel left his role as CTO. Elon Musk has published a couple of somewhat scattered, rambling “master plans,” but we haven’t gotten any significant new products aside from the Cybertruck and the just arriving Cybercab.

Even looking over on the energy storage side of things, the Tesla Megapack was launched in July 2019, the month Straubel stepped down from his role as CTO. Did Straubel just decide he had done enough once he had finished the Megapack launch and gotten the Model Y essentially ready for market? Did he have conflicts with Musk on where to take the company from there?

Yes, there’s been incremental product development and refreshed versions of Tesla cars and energy storage systems. There are still plenty of engineers working on improving things. However, there doesn’t seem to be the same leadership in new product development, and there also isn’t the same practical, moderating element that Straubel seemingly provided to Musk’s more wild, grandiose, sci-fi inspired dreams and ideas.

raw_title: Why Some Drivers Hand Police A Blue Envelope During A Traffic Stop
title: Why Some Drivers Hand Police A Blue Envelope During A Traffic Stop
raw_summary: Getting pulled over is never a fun time. The reasons are seemingly endless, from driving a police magnet to dangling a keepsake from the rearview mirror or having Flock misidentify your car as stolen . Now imagine going through any of these scenarios while also having a disability that creates communication challenges, such as autism. For someone with sensory, cognitive, and verbal difficulties, the already stressful event of being pulled over could lead to trauma or even being shot. And for the police officer, being unaware of the driver's medical condition can lead to miscommunication and mishandling of the situation. That's why the Blue Envelope Program was developed: to improve communication between law enforcement and people who require additional accommodations or time during stops. Designed to be an all-inclusive information tool that's easy and straightforward to use for both the driver and officer, on the envelope's exterior are printed instructions and guidelines regarding how to interact with one another, while inside are essential documents, such as a driver's license, proof of insurance, and vehicle registration.

article_paragraphs: Getting pulled over is never a fun time. The reasons are seemingly endless, from driving a police magnet to dangling a keepsake from the rearview mirror or having Flock misidentify your car as stolen . Now imagine going through any of these scenarios while also having a disability that creates communication challenges, such as autism. For someone with sensory, cognitive, and verbal difficulties, the already stressful event of being pulled over could lead to trauma or even being shot. And for the police officer, being unaware of the driver's medical condition can lead to miscommunication and mishandling of the situation.

That's why the Blue Envelope Program was developed: to improve communication between law enforcement and people who require additional accommodations or time during stops. Designed to be an all-inclusive information tool that's easy and straightforward to use for both the driver and officer, on the envelope's exterior are printed instructions and guidelines regarding how to interact with one another, while inside are essential documents, such as a driver's license, proof of insurance, and vehicle registration.

To improve awareness and reduce stress for drivers with Autism Spectrum Disorder, Connecticut created the first Blue Envelope program by state law in 2020. As of February 2026, per the Organization for Autism Research it had been adopted statewide or locally in 30 states. Of those, 13 have made such communication a statewide effort, reports the National Conference of State Legislatures : Arizona, Arkansas, Connecticut, Florida, Idaho, Indiana, Mississippi, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Rhode Island, Tennessee and Virginia.

Using the color blue, or even envelopes, is not universal, however. The envelope color can vary based on jurisdiction and medical condition. The legislature group says blue is generally used to signify an autism diagnosis, yellow is displayed for those with communication impediments, and green signifies a mental illness. Arkansas, for example, provides both blue and green envelopes based on a person's condition and needs.

Then you have states that distribute decals instead to inform police and first responders about a driver's extra needs. Florida, Idaho, Indiana, Nevada, New Jersey and Tennessee use yellow-dot stickers, applied either to the driver's license or the vehicle. Arizona's program requires that the decal be 3½ inches in diameter with "saving lives" imprinted in the center and affixed to the upper left corner of the vehicle's rear window. Beyond that, though, there is no set standard on where these identifying dots are placed, only that they are visible to instantly inform responders to approach the driver with patience and care.

Autism was first recognized in 1943 by scientist Leo Kanner. According to the Autism Science Foundation , "autism" is a catchall phrase for a neurological condition in which people can display apathy in social settings, insist on routine, and exhibit repetitive behaviors like rocking or flapping their hands. Some cases of autism may involve aggression or self-injury. The foundation says about 40% also include a cognitive disability.

Although available science suggests a genetic origin, there's no single known cause for autism, which is found in all cultures, races, regions, and ethnic groups. Boys are four times more likely to be affected than girls, but characteristics vary greatly from individual to individual. Without a single distinctive trait, people with autism aren't obvious, which is why programs like Blue Envelope need to be the first line of communication with officers or EMTs. If not for this context, a person's lack of eye contact, rapid movements, or unresponsiveness to directions could be misinterpreted as disobeying an officer or resisting arrest.

Laws don't need to be enacted to improve traffic stop safety for people with autism. Local law-enforcement agencies can organize Blue Envelope programs without needing state authorization. And for participants, diagnosis documentation isn't required to obtain a color-coded envelope or decal, which are readily available through motor-vehicle registries, police departments, driving schools, and advocacy groups in places that have adopted the program.

title: New Honda Avancier Hybrid SUV Teased, Global Debut Expected On December 1
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The upcoming model will introduce the company’s next-generation hybrid technology and a fresh design language Honda has released the first teaser of the new Avancier, an upcoming hybrid SUV expected to make its global debut on December 1, 2026. The new model is reportedly being developed as a seven-seater and will sit above the CR-V in Honda’s international lineup. It is expected to be manufactured in Thailand, with Australia and several Asian markets among its likely destinations. The Avancier name isn’t entirely new. Honda first used it for an Accord-based station wagon sold in Japan between 1999 and 2003. The name returned in 2016 on a crossover SUV developed for the Chinese market. This latest model, however, appears to be a completely different vehicle, designed for a wider international audience. The teaser keeps most of the SUV hidden, but there are a few interesting details. Up front, the Avancier gets slim LED daytime running lights with an animated lighting sequence. The main headlamp units appear to sit lower down, giving it a split-headlamp arrangement. At the rear, a horizontal LED light bar stretches across the tailgate and connects with vertical lighting elements at either end. The design creates a distinctive H-shaped signature, complemented by Honda’s new corporate emblem and Avancier lettering. Also Read: Honda 0 Alpha Electric SUV To Debut In India On December 2, 2026 The SUV also appears to have a relatively long body, a sharply defined shoulder line and a sloping rear windscreen. Despite its large proportions, the overall silhouette looks more like a raised estate than a conventional boxy SUV. Reports suggest that the Avancier could measure approximately 4,960 mm in length, 1,950 mm in width and 1,690 mm in height. These dimensions are yet to be officially confirmed. One of the more important details confirmed in the teaser is the new Honda Hybrid branding. The Avancier is expected to be among the first production models to use Honda’s next-generation hybrid system, which builds on the technology currently offered under the e name. The new system is expected to use a revised 2.0-litre petrol engine paired with electric motors. Reports also suggest that an electric all-wheel-drive setup could be offered, although Honda has not confirmed the powertrain configuration. Also Read: 4 All-New Cars Set To Launch In November 2026 In India Honda has previously outlined plans to introduce 15 next-generation hybrid models globally by the end of March 2030. The Avancier appears to be one of the first products under that strategy. The new Avancier is expected to be positioned above the CR-V and compete internationally with SUVs such as the Hyundai Santa Fe, Kia Sorento and Mazda CX-80. Honda has not announced any plans to introduce the Avancier in India. With the model reportedly being developed for right-hand-drive markets and production expected in Thailand, an Indian launch cannot be ruled out, but there is no confirmation at this stage. More details about the SUV’s interior, hybrid powertrain and market availability should emerge at its expected December 1 unveiling.

raw_title: 7 Hybrids With Some Of The Worst MPG Ratings
title: 7 Hybrids With Some Of The Worst MPG Ratings
raw_summary: Thanks to vehicles like the Toyota Prius, the term hybrid is often associated with cars that get very good fuel economy. For the most part, this notion proves true. The latest Prius has a combined fuel economy rating of 55 mpg, which goes a long way when a regular gallon of gas is $4.26, as of the time of this writing. Yet, not every hybrid is a fuel-sipper. Some manufacturers use hybrid technology to increase engine power, while others opt for electrification as a way of squeezing extra efficiency out of inherently inefficient vehicles. While many hybrids could be classified as inefficient, we chose ones with a combined EPA fuel economy rating below 20 mpg. To put the number in perspective, the average new vehicle for the 2024 model year, which includes all vehicle types, was rated at 27.2 mpg combined. Whether fuel economy ratings match reality is a subject for another conversation. All of the ratings we'll mention reflect a combined mpg, unless noted otherwise.

While many hybrids could be classified as inefficient, we chose ones with a combined EPA fuel economy rating below 20 mpg. To put the number in perspective, the average new vehicle for the 2024 model year, which includes all vehicle types, was rated at 27.2 mpg combined. Whether fuel economy ratings match reality is a subject for another conversation. All of the ratings we'll mention reflect a combined mpg, unless noted otherwise.

Our list includes exotics like the Lamborghini Revuelto and Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X, as well as SUVs with sports-car intentions like the Audi RS Q8, BMW X5 M Competition, and Mercedes-AMG GLS 63. The Toyota Tundra also makes the cut. In case you're a fan of nostalgia, let's not forget the Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Hybrid. Spoiler alert: almost all of these are rated at 16 mpg or below.

It's not a significant stretch that a three-ton flagship pickup lands on our list highlighting hybrids with the worst fuel economy. At least we can call the Tundra the most efficient of the least efficient. It's the TRD Pro that deserves this special recognition. Most Tundra trims with the twin-turbocharged 3.4 liter V6 and hybrid setup manage to crack the 20 mpg threshold. However, the TRD Pro's off-road running gear is the likely reason behind its 1 mpg penalty. At 19 mpg, this is the only vehicle among the group to top 16 mpg.

The Tundra TRD Pro's upgraded powerplant produces a combined 437 horsepower and 583 lb-ft of torque. Consider that the previous second generation's V8 engine maxed out at 381 horsepower. Additionally, the third-generation Tundra's i-Force Max unit hasn't been caught up in Toyota's notorious V6 engine recall , and its parallel hybrid system incorporates an electric motor between the engine and transmission. This parallel layout helps maximize power and torque, with fuel conservation being an added benefit.

In case you weren't following General Motors' powertrain development two decades ago, the automaker dabbled in hybrid systems for some of its largest vehicles, including the Silverado 1500. The 2005 retail debut (with some fleet deliveries in 2004) featured a 295-horsepower 5.3-liter V8 engine paired with a unique electrical system to support start-stop and save fuel rather than power motion. Confined to an extended cab configuration with either rear-wheel drive (RWD) or four-wheel drive (4WD), the arrangement offered up to a 1-2 mpg boost in fuel economy over the non-hybrid 5.3-liter V8 engine. With the hybrid setup, EPA ratings were 17 mpg for RWD and 16 mpg for 4WD.

General Motors also offered this hybrid technology in the GMC Sierra. Reportedly, the hybrid Silverado and Sierra versions had an entire production run of about 3,000, making this more of a marketing exercise. GM would launch a more efficient hybrid system for the 2009 model year, which also introduced an electrified Cadillac Escalade.

The 2024 Audi RS Q8 follows a familiar formula for premium German marques: stuff abundant power into an everyday vehicle. In this case, it's a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 engine making 591 horsepower, a setup that started when the model debuted in 2020. Audi also adds a mild-hybrid system to the mix. This technology can't power the car on electricity alone, but is used (via a small electric motor and battery) to recover braking energy. Mild hybrids are especially popular among European brands.

title: BMW Has Two Laboratories Dedicated To Ensuring Its Cars Smell Good
raw_summary: As someone who makes a living evaluating and commenting on the business of automobiles, I've always felt that how the things smell is an underreported aspect that the media should pay more attention to. Yeah, it may be hard to convey smells through a video, let alone text, but the same could arguably be said about driving dynamics, and no car reviewer worth their salt is turning their nose up at covering that. The reality, however, is that interior smells can account for a whole lot of how a car is perceived , and automakers know this. Luxury brands like BMW, in fact, have dedicated teams and facilities that make sure the insides of those factory-fresh Bimmers smell just right, and Audi is known to do something similar. According to BMW Blog , the Bavarian brand has operated an "odor laboratory" in its hometown of Munich, Germany, since 1999, and in 2014, it opened a second one in Shenyang, China.

article_paragraphs: As someone who makes a living evaluating and commenting on the business of automobiles, I've always felt that how the things smell is an underreported aspect that the media should pay more attention to. Yeah, it may be hard to convey smells through a video, let alone text, but the same could arguably be said about driving dynamics, and no car reviewer worth their salt is turning their nose up at covering that.

The reality, however, is that interior smells can account for a whole lot of how a car is perceived , and automakers know this. Luxury brands like BMW, in fact, have dedicated teams and facilities that make sure the insides of those factory-fresh Bimmers smell just right, and Audi is known to do something similar. According to BMW Blog , the Bavarian brand has operated an "odor laboratory" in its hometown of Munich, Germany, since 1999, and in 2014, it opened a second one in Shenyang, China.

The BMW staff who work in these odor labs are apparently known as the "nose team" and spend their days sniffing interior plastics, leathers, fabrics, and adhesives to minimize bad odors and ensure optimal air quality inside new vehicles. Each new interior apparently must go through a three-stage validation process: one that focuses on materials themselves, one for individual components like dashboards, door cards, and seats, then one final assessment that accounts for the entire assembled car. In the earlier stages, parts are placed inside emission and climatic chambers and exposed to high temps to simulate, say, a BMW being parked outside in the summer sun.

Some "nose team" decisions have apparently included steel speaker grilles instead of comparatively smelly plastic, and animal-derived proteins are apparently avoided since natural leathers tend to give off a worse scent as they age. A brand new luxury car's leather may smell great, but older luxury rides often smell like somebody's old couch (and not in a good way). That new BMW smell is purely the product of all the materials inside intermingling, with no artificial perfumes or tricks used.

Of course, you don't have to be into cars to know what a new car is supposed to smell like. Little Trees literally makes air fresheners that mimic that "new car smell." What you're actually smelling as you drive away from the dealership is a cocktail of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) being released by the materials inside the cabin. By definition, not all VOCs are harmful or carcinogenic. However, a 2023 study by researchers at Harvard and the Beijing Institute of Technology found that some of the ones responsible for that distinctive new car scent could be linked to increased cancer risk . The study identified formaldehyde and acetaldehyde as among the potentially hazardous compounds released. A separate 2021 study by UC Riverside came to a similar conclusion.

BMW's odor labs seem to take the health factor of interior emissions just as seriously as making the inside of that new 3 Series pleasing to sniff. In the interest of healthier interiors, one material choice made by BMW's "nose team" is new microfibers that are said to minimize these VOCs, aldehydes, and fogging substances.
All that sounds great if you're in the market for a BMW, but the company's work at these odor labs could benefit the wider industry. Apparently, BMW says it shares findings with other automakers.

"We are doing this job with emissions inside a car and materials for more than 25 years," said interior air quality and evaporative emissions manager Andreas Wehrmeier. "So we take a leading role and gladly share our knowledge with others to bring everybody forward so that every car in the world is safe, and not just a BMW."

raw_title: These Are Some Of The Most Annoying Passenger Habits, According To Uber Drivers
title: These Are Some Of The Most Annoying Passenger Habits, According To Uber Drivers
raw_summary: Driving for Uber has its perks. You pick your hours, can earn more with bonuses and promotions, and don't even need to own a car. If you do own a car and it's less than 15 years old and in good working order, it will likely fit the bill to be used as an Uber. But with every pro, there is a con. Beyond the continued conflict with taxi cab companies, rideshare drivers have had to unionize for employee rights and benefits, sued over wage theft, face increasing costs , and are asked to equip their vehicles as AI-training data gatherers for robotaxis that will eventually replace them. Whew.

article_paragraphs: Driving for Uber has its perks. You pick your hours, can earn more with bonuses and promotions, and don't even need to own a car. If you do own a car and it's less than 15 years old and in good working order, it will likely fit the bill to be used as an Uber. But with every pro, there is a con.

Beyond the continued conflict with taxi cab companies, rideshare drivers have had to unionize for employee rights and benefits, sued over wage theft, face increasing costs , and are asked to equip their vehicles as AI-training data gatherers for robotaxis that will eventually replace them. Whew.

Along with these big picture problems, in the car, drivers experience the good, bad, and ugly habits of riders, like tipping. Service industry workers understand that good service equals good tips. A reality Uber drivers encounter is receiving praise and the promise of a reward but, ultimately, getting no tip. According to a rideshare survey conducted by travel site Upgraded Points , nearly 20 percent of rideshare users surprisingly do this. Interestingly, the survey included over 3,100 rideshare passengers who admitted to this and other less-than-courteous behaviors.

There are millions of reasons why someone would order a rideshare but almost none to warrant being an irritating, rude, or downright terrible passenger. There are a plethora of passenger pet peeves for drivers (why do people behave so badly?). Some are expected, like riders who talk too much, but others are a bit more disconcerting, unsafe, or downright shocking.

We compiled this list of graceless examples through Upgraded Points' survey results as well as reports from drivers via Reddit , community resources such as Ride.Guru and The Rideshare Guy , and Uber's own Community Guidelines . Annoying passenger habits fall under five main categories: rude behavior, poor planning, safety, children and safety, and being gross, both literally and smarmily. Thankfully, there are several ways Uber drivers can deal with terrible riders before, during, and after a trip.

Many of the annoyances of rideshare drivers are similar to common frustrations of frequent fliers . An Uber driver can be stuck in their car with the human embodiment of a nightmare. Many of their grievances have to do with rude behavior and being disrespected. Passengers who show up late, are rude, exhibit anger, smoke in the vehicle, eat and drink without permission...basically anything but being courteous.

Chatty Kathys are a notable bane of many. An oversharing passenger can be overbearing, but so can a silent rider by creating an awkward atmosphere. The Ridseshare Guy mentions speakerphone offenders being problematic for multiple reasons. First, many drivers record video of their rides so that the conversation could have a life after they disconnect. And even if not on speaker, there are oblivious riders who have intimate talks or share private information, like credit card info, while riding.

There are instances of riders reaching over and touching radios or plugging in their phones to play music, all without asking if they can do so. Uber drivers on Reddit say being inconsiderate of the driver's car won't win you favorite passenger points. Not all drivers are okay with riders traveling with food either. If they are, don't expect to be allowed to eat your takeout order or leftovers while commuting. Others don't allow drinks at all. This includes alcohol or even bottled water because how does a driver know that clear liquid is, in fact, water?

title: A New $1.5 Billion Wind Farm Will Play In Peoria
raw_summary: It ain’t over ’til it’s over, but the proposed $1.5 billion, 500-megawatt Four Creeks wind farm in Peoria County, Illinois has just passed a key step in the approval process. The new milestone is yet another indication that the domestic wind industry will continue to play a key role in the US energy transition, regardless of the topsy-turvy energy policy articulated by US President Donald Trump. If you’re somewhat shocked to hear word of a new wind farm proposal in the US, join the club. The President has spent considerable time, energy, and taxpayer dollars in a Herculean effort to keep new wind turbines from cropping up around the US under his watch. However, his efforts have earned only mixed success so far.

The new milestone is yet another indication that the domestic wind industry will continue to play a key role in the US energy transition, regardless of the topsy-turvy energy policy articulated by US President Donald Trump.
article_paragraphs: It ain’t over ’til it’s over, but the proposed $1.5 billion, 500-megawatt Four Creeks wind farm in Peoria County, Illinois has just passed a key step in the approval process. The new milestone is yet another indication that the domestic wind industry will continue to play a key role in the US energy transition, regardless of the topsy-turvy energy policy articulated by US President Donald Trump.

If you’re somewhat shocked to hear word of a new wind farm proposal in the US, join the club. The President has spent considerable time, energy, and taxpayer dollars in a Herculean effort to keep new wind turbines from cropping up around the US under his watch. However, his efforts have earned only mixed success so far.

Offshore wind turbine s keep slipping through the cracks, even though virtually every offshore wind farm in the US is subject to federal authority. Opportunities for wind power also persist on land, where the President’s direct authority is limited to projects on federal property.

Trump attempted to work around that obstacle in August of 2025, when he weaponized an otherwise routine wind project review process that applies to projects on non-federal property. The change in policy threw at least 155 onshore wind projects totaling 45 gigawatts into limbo, prompting a lawsuit from a coalition of clean energy organizations and wind energy developers.

In July of this year, Attorneys General in 19 states intervened in support of the lawsuit. The participants included Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Illinois, Maine, Massachusetts, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, and Washington State.

Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul, who co-led the intervention, notes that federal law does require wind developers to submit proposals for wind turbines more than 200 feet tall to the Federal Aviation Administration, which then refers the project to DoD to check for any conflicts with military operations and related activities. Raoul further notes that the normal process involves collaborating on mitigation measures to resolve any conflicts.

That all ground to a halt in August of 2025, when DoD dropped the ball on its part of the process. “Officials ceased countersigning mitigation agreements, stopped sending completed agreements to developers for signature, and delayed or halted communications with developers about mitigation,” Raoul explained in a press statement in July.
The abrupt change in policy impacted at least nine wind projects in Illinois alone. According to Raoul’s office the nine projects represent $4.3 billion in private investment, or more.

raw_title: Why Russell's 'pole' was lost either way
title: Why Russell's 'pole' was lost either way
raw_summary: George Russell knew he would not start the 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix from pole position due to a grid penalty, yet missing out on being quickest left him feeling unusually hurt regardless. Russell ended the delayed, wet Interlagos qualifying session convinced his Mercedes Formula 1 team had made him abandon a lap that was “definitely” going to be quickest.
summary: George Russell knew he would not start the 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix from pole position due to a grid penalty, yet missing out on being quickest left him feeling unusually hurt regardless. Russell ended the delayed, wet Interlagos qualifying session convinced his Mercedes Formula 1 team had made him abandon a lap that was “definitely” going to be quickest.
article_paragraphs: George Russell knew he would not start the 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix from pole position due to a grid penalty, yet missing out on being quickest left him feeling unusually hurt regardless.
Russell ended the delayed, wet Interlagos qualifying session convinced his Mercedes Formula 1 team had made him abandon a lap that was “definitely” going to be quickest.

That certainty was understandable, but probably overzealous. He would never have started from pole anyway, thanks to his five-place grid drop, but he was poised to miss out regardless of backing off because the lap was almost certainly about to be inadvertently compromised by Russell’s good friend Alex Albon.
What hurt Russell so much, though, was the loss of something deeper – a rare moment of obvious superiority in a season that promised so much and yet has been so disappointing.

The only reason Russell’s race engineer Marcus Dudley advised him to back off was because Russell had caught Alex Albon’s Williams – and Russell had even complained about Albon being in his way in the middle of the lap.

While Russell did seem to be on his way to completing a faster lap than eventual polesitter Lando Norris, as he was at least a few hundredths quicker at the moment he aborted, that relies on a clear run to end the lap that Russell would not have had.

Russell was close enough to Albon that he had already posted three mini-sectors in a row slower than his previous lap. He would have potentially been disturbed through the left-hand Turn 11 at the end of the middle sector, then the Juncao left-hander that leads to the long, uphill run to the finish line, and the kink onto the start-finish straight.
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said Russell was “very slightly up on Norris at that point but was catching Albon and we thought was about to lose time”. And the threat was real.

raw_summary: A proper wet weather qualifying session was always going to produce some colossal performances, and some outings to forget, too. Here are our winners and losers from a bonkers session, which featured everything from zeroes to heroes.
summary: A proper wet weather qualifying session was always going to produce some colossal performances, and some outings to forget, too. Here are our winners and losers from a bonkers session, which featured everything from zeroes to heroes.
article_paragraphs: A proper wet weather qualifying session was always going to produce some colossal performances, and some outings to forget, too.
Here are our winners and losers from a bonkers session, which featured everything from zeroes to heroes.
Russell’s simmering rage could have dried half of the Interlagos track on its own after he aborted what he felt was definitely going to be the pole position lap.
It almost certainly wasn’t. He was very slightly up on Lando Norris’s lap, but was set to be contained by Alex Albon’s Williams in the final sector, where Russell would have lost a heap of time.
And he wouldn’t have started on pole anyway due to a five-place grid penalty.
But you could tell this session meant more to Russell than the position he’d actually have at the end of it.

Russell was fast, all the time, and quicker than Kimi Antonelli. He wanted to make it count. He still did, mostly. But after losing the championship, all the talk about his bad luck, and the frustrating reality that he's too often been second-best, this was looking like a rare win.

It should still be, really. For him to come out of it so unhappy, though, and with a seventh-place start when he was probably the quickest driver out there, is an underserved loss. - Scott Mitchell-Malm

title: Of course there is tension
raw_summary: As Lewis Hamilton and Fred Vasseur have faced a barrage of questions about Ferrari’s Mexican Grand Prix debacle in Brazil, and what needs to be done to ensure Hamilton and Charles Leclerc can actually race one another without hurting the team’s interests, Leclerc’s view has been basically absent from the debate. He’s been understandably late to this discussion, owing to the birth of his first child this past week, and in his own words “the time where I've had Bianca in my arms, there wasn't much more or much else in my head, and that's been the case until probably Thursday night when I arrived and when it was time to speak with Fred and Lewis”.

He’s been understandably late to this discussion, owing to the birth of his first child this past week, and in his own words “the time where I've had Bianca in my arms, there wasn't much more or much else in my head, and that's been the case until probably Thursday night when I arrived and when it was time to speak with Fred and Lewis”.

There was a brief comment in the media pen after Friday practice, when Leclerc said he considered the matter “fully settled” following those internal talks, and that “I don’t think we should be speaking about it too much going forward”.
After qualifying on Saturday Leclerc had to field several more questions aimed at getting him to open up on this matter, and he pretty much stuck to the same script.
“From my perspective I was very straightforward of course and I think it was good to speak,” he said. “I think this is always needed after a moment like this.
“I think it took proportions that are way too big, but it has been around also for way too long.

“At the same time it was a very special week for me so I couldn't really have those discussions before and it was important to have those discussions, but now I consider that a closed chapter and I think it will be important to look ahead.”

But as much as Leclerc was trying to move the F1 world on from what happened last Sunday in Mexico, he also in the same breath confirmed the competitive tension between himself and Hamilton that Vasseur is surely going to have his work cut out trying to manage.
