Marquez and Bezzecchi came together on the fourth lap of the race after a red-flag restart, as Marquez - running ahead of the Aprilia rider - left room on the corner apex by taking a wider line than Bezzecchi.
article_paragraphs: Reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez took another step towards the 2026 title after winning the Qatar Grand Prix sprint - following a controversial collision with Marco Bezzecchi.

Marquez and Bezzecchi came together on the fourth lap of the race after a red-flag restart, as Marquez - running ahead of the Aprilia rider - left room on the corner apex by taking a wider line than Bezzecchi.
Bezzecchi tried to sneak past on the apex, but as Marquez returned to the racing line the pair collided - and Bezzecchi's Aprilia slid out from under him.
The incident was investigated by the stewards, but they quickly took no further action, to the seeming discontent of Aprilia racing boss Massimo Rivola as he learned of the verdict on the broadcast.

In the original race start, Bezzecchi had headed Marquez from pole, but the race was neutralised for a major crash involving Fermin Aldeguer and Pecco Bagnaia.
Bagnaia had briefly featured in second place but was shuffled down to fifth, before being struck from behind by Aldeguer - who was in the process of lunging at Pedro Acosta for sixth.
Bagnaia was taken to the medical centre and did not take part in the restart.

title: Foot fractures for Bagnaia after scary Qatar sprint crash
raw_summary: Ducati MotoGP rider Pecco Bagnaia has been diagnosed with a foot fracture after his scary Qatar Grand Prix sprint crash. Two-time series champion Bagnaia had been up to as high as second at the beginning of the race, but had dropped back down to fifth by the time the accident happened.
summary: Ducati MotoGP rider Pecco Bagnaia has been diagnosed with a foot fracture after his scary Qatar Grand Prix sprint crash. Two-time series champion Bagnaia had been up to as high as second at the beginning of the race, but had dropped back down to fifth by the time the accident happened.
article_paragraphs: Ducati MotoGP rider Pecco Bagnaia has been diagnosed with a foot fracture after his scary Qatar Grand Prix sprint crash.
Two-time series champion Bagnaia had been up to as high as second at the beginning of the race, but had dropped back down to fifth by the time the accident happened.
Fellow Ducati rider Fermin Aldeguer had launched an attack on KTM's Pedro Acosta behind Bagnaia at Turn 16 and ended up piling into Bagnaia's bike, sending him into a vicious highside.
Bagnaia was seemingly briefly knocked unconscious by the impact, though was apparently back to consciousness when attended to in the gravel trap.

He was stretchered away from the site of the incident as the race was red-flagged. A subsequent medical centre examination revealed a double fracture in Bagnaia's right foot, and he will be transferred to Doha Hospital for further examination and treatment.
Ducati said the two fractures "involved the fourth and fifth metatarsals" and that whether Bagnaia would have surgery or not would be determined at the hospital.
It has not communicated whether Bagnaia was officially ruled out of the grand prix race on Sunday - though this seems highly likely.
Aldeguer was handed a double long lap penalty for causing the collision, which he served after the red flag in the restarted sprint. He finished the race in 11th.

raw_summary: One of the most loved Japanese sports cars of the 21st century is the Nissan 350Z, partly because it was one of the badass villain cars in "The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift." But there's more to it than just that. While looks are subjective, it's hard to deny that it has aged rather nicely. It's also still genuinely affordable, making it one of the cheaper alternatives to Japanese performance cars that have skyrocketed in value . In essence, it's a 3.5-liter naturally aspirated V6 that produces around 287 horsepower in early 350Zs (or closer to 300 hp in the Nismo versions). That's fast enough to red-face some of the greatest sport sedans of all time .

article_paragraphs: One of the most loved Japanese sports cars of the 21st century is the Nissan 350Z, partly because it was one of the badass villain cars in "The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift." But there's more to it than just that. While looks are subjective, it's hard to deny that it has aged rather nicely. It's also still genuinely affordable, making it one of the cheaper alternatives to Japanese performance cars that have skyrocketed in value .

But perhaps the main reason for its celebrated status is its engine: Nissan's VQ35. In essence, it's a 3.5-liter naturally aspirated V6 that produces around 287 horsepower in early 350Zs (or closer to 300 hp in the Nismo versions). Even by today's standards, the 350Z is quick: in Car and Driver 's testing, 0 to 60 miles per hour took 5.4 seconds, and it didn't top out until 156 mph. That's fast enough to red-face some of the greatest sport sedans of all time .

The good news doesn't stop there either, because the VQ35 is also famed for its reliability, despite oil consumption issues. As with anything mechanical, it does depend on how well you treat and maintain it, but do so properly, and you're likely in for one hell of an ownership experience.

Nissan made a few sound decisions right off the bat, like opting against turbocharging and keeping the engine naturally aspirated. (Of course, a naturally aspirated engine has fewer moving parts and is therefore generally considered better for durability.) The VQ35 also uses timing chains rather than timing belts. Timing chains are generally considered to be more durable than timing belts – they don't have a defined replacement period and can often last as long as the engine itself.

Thanks to a crankshaft and connecting rods made of forged steel, the VQ35 can deal with high-RPM loads and long-term wear and tear better than engines that use regular cast-metal internals. On top of that, the engine block and cylinder heads are made from aluminum alloy, which is famous for both its thermal conductivity and its resistance to corrosion. The pistons are also coated with a molybdenum-based lubricant, which helps reduce friction.

Aside from the 350Z, another notable host of the VQ35 is the Skyline. No, we're not talking about Nissan's most famous performance car ever , but about the subtle sedan that began life in 2001 as the 11th-generation Skyline, and eventually spawned a sportier GT-focused version called the 350GT. In North America, it was sold under the Infiniti badge.

Other famous Nissans to use the VQ35 include the second-generation Stagea 350RX, which is arguably one of the best wagons of all time , and the Nissan Maxima , which used this superb engine right up to its final model year (2023). You might also be interested to know the VQ35 made its way into several racing cars, albeit with some major alterations. Those include the 2009 Renault Megane Trophy and even Dallara's T05 and T08 open-wheel cars from the Formula Renault 3.5 Series. So, gained some more respect for this old buster?

title: Tesla deemed liable for fraud after Solar Roof 'experiment' on a home
raw_summary: A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a Solar Roof lawsuit, after the company repeatedly failed to hand over evidence. Tesla had already admitted it breached the contract, broke its warranty, and was negligent on the job. The homeowner says fixing the damage will cost “well over $2.5 million.” Tesla once offered him $5,000.
summary: A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a Solar Roof lawsuit, after the company repeatedly failed to hand over evidence. Tesla had already admitted it breached the contract, broke its warranty, and was negligent on the job. The homeowner says fixing the damage will cost “well over $2.5 million.” Tesla once offered him $5,000.
article_paragraphs: A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a Solar Roof lawsuit, after the company repeatedly failed to hand over evidence. Tesla had already admitted it breached the contract, broke its warranty, and was negligent on the job.
The homeowner says fixing the damage will cost “well over $2.5 million.” Tesla once offered him $5,000.

The case is Conroy v. Tesla , filed in 2022 in San Diego Superior Court’s North County division (case No. 37-2022-00043670). Electrek reviewed the court orders, the complaint, and the parties’ joint trial readiness report. Here’s what’s in them.

Ambrose Conroy, who lives in Rancho Santa Fe, signed up for a Tesla Solar Roof in March 2020. The original contract was $82,210 for a 13.1 kW system. By February 2021, after two amendments, it had grown to roughly $110,000 for an 18.2 kW roof and six Powerwalls.
The roof was never finished. It never passed a county inspection, and it never produced a single kWh for the house.
Tesla isn’t contesting most of that anymore. In the joint report filed by both sides last month, Tesla stipulated to liability on three of the five claims.
The other two claims, fraud and negligent misrepresentation, are where things went badly for Tesla.

Judge Cynthia Freeland sanctioned Tesla twice over discovery before going further. She ordered it to pay $15,467.50 in February and another $13,500 in June, both times for failing to produce a proper privilege log and responsive documents, and both times warning that issue sanctions could follow.

raw_title: This Focus RS Makes Us Nostalgic for a Time When Ford Built Cars Besides the Mustang
title: This Focus RS Makes Us Nostalgic for a Time When Ford Built Cars Besides the Mustang
raw_summary: Ford killed off the Focus globally just last year, much to the chagrin of anyone who enjoyed a scrappy little hatchback or sedan with a blue oval up front. Sure, the Mustang is still around, but the Focus and the Fiesta provided an entirely different kind of Fast Ford, compact performance that you could use every day. And there was one Focus trim that was the best of them all. Here’s a nearly new example of maximum Focus: a 2016 Focus RS with just 2200 miles on the odometer, for sale on Bring a Trailer (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos). It’s a single-owner, garage-kept car from Texas, and for those in colder climes, it happens to have been optioned with the RS2 package that includes heated seats and a heated steering wheel. Slap on a set of snow tires, and get ready to shred this upcoming winter.

It’s a single-owner, garage-kept car from Texas, and for those in colder climes, it happens to have been optioned with the RS2 package that includes heated seats and a heated steering wheel. Slap on a set of snow tires, and get ready to shred this upcoming winter.
See all results for used 2016 Ford Focus RS for sale near 20147

Pairing a 350-hp 2.3-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine with a six-speed manual gearbox and clever all-wheel drive, the Focus RS was basically Ford’s answer to the Subaru STI and the Mitsubishi Lancer EVO. WRC champion Colin McRae did spend quite a bit of time rallying in Fords, and that heritage was baked right into the RS, even if U.S. fans weren’t as broadly familiar with the world of rally.

For those who were, the RS was a revelation. The punchy four built boost quickly, and it somehow had far more turbo personality than when it appeared in the EcoBoost version of the Mustang. The all-wheel drive was even better, equipped with the ability to direct as much as 70 percent of the power to either outside rear wheel. With understeer thus banished, the RS could tear up a winding back road with a pace equal to far more expensive machines.

And yes, it came with Drift mode. Fully unlock this ability by switching off traction control, and the Focus RS can lay down Ken Block–style tire-smoking slides with ease. Not great for your tire budget, but huge fun nonetheless.

The only drawback was trying to get your hands on one when new, as dealers often tried to add considerable markup to the price tag. This example, painted a laid-back Stealth Gray, flies under the radar a bit and is just waiting for an owner who is going to pack on the miles.

In a low-key color, and with only hints of the performance peeking out from that hatchback shape in the form of a rear wing and blue Brembo brakes, this RS is a bit of an if-you-know-then-you-know car. It’s a real shame that Ford doesn’t sell anything like it anymore. On the other hand, that just makes this one that much more special.

Schuppan, whose resume includes a victory at Le Mans in 1983, a bronze medal at the ’81 Indianapolis 500, and experience on the Formula 1 tour, plans to build 50 of these Team Schuppan 962s. That’s 962, as in Porsche Official Race Car, twice the winner at Le Mans and three times an IMSA season champion.

With all sorts of real and imagined race-cars-for-the-road getting serious ink these days, Schuppan has been doing in­stead of promising. The 47-year-old Aus­tralian has this Le Mans long-tailed 962 li­censed and fully certified for the road and, as this is written, is close to complet­ing the first of what is to be a limited se­ries of Team Schuppan 962CRs (the no­menclature is “C” for Group C and “R” for road) on the same basis but with unique “GT” bodywork and all the com­fort features one might expect for more than 1.5 million dollars.

Because this project has been commissioned by a Japanese outfit—Art Sport Division, a company that specializes in exotic machinery and is headed by Toshio Terada—most of them will be measured in yen, 220 million or there­abouts. The company says it will sell the first 50 worldwide, with seventeen head­ed for America. The red car shown on these pages is also destined for Japan, for the garage of Hiroyuki Miyake, a real-estate executive and Schuppan racing sponsor who want­ed a Le Mans racer with the minimum of modifications needed to make it street-­legal. A genuine Stuttgart-built 962 (number 962/123), it started life in IMSA with the Primus team. Schuppan rebuilt it as a Group C car with a British-made aluminum honeycomb chassis and took it to Le Mans in 1988, where it was driven by Brian Redman, Jean-Pierre Jarier, and Eje Elgh. It ran sixth for a while and fin­ished tenth. After competing in the Fuji 1000-kilometer race that year, the car was retired. When Schuppan began pon­dering the notion of a roadgoing 962 some twenty months ago, it was there at the back of the shop, a suitable case for treatment.

This is a real-life racer, currently designated as a 962R, and is the prototype for Team Schuppan’s road rockets, the first of which should roll out the doors in Octo­ber. The work done on this car will be ap­plied directly to the “CR” street car, which, unlike this “R” model, will have its nose and headlight area smoothed and finished. (Miyake’s enthusiasm has gen­erated two more orders for replicas of this Le Mans car, so Schuppan now has plans to build five of them in addition to the 50 street cars. They will sell for the same price as the more comfortably equipped GT version.)

All of the “production” models will have Schuppan’s own carbon-fiber monocoque chassis, developed for his 962 race cars, and carbon-fiber and Kevlar bodywork instead of the original Porsche panels, which are mostly fiberglass.

Driving a full-spec Group C car on normal roads should not be a problem—­if the pavement is smooth. But bringing one into compliance with all of the appli­cable regulations is something else. Rather more, in fact, than Vern Schup­pan and his friend and associate Howden Ganley (another ex-racer from Down Under and the man behind the Tiga race-car company) had thought when they embarked on the venture.

The good news is it will be a very short line in the United States, with room for only seventeen.

raw_summary: Both Ferrari drivers will take 10-place grid penalties at Formula 1’s Brazilian Grand Prix for new internal combustion engines. article_paragraphs: Both Ferrari drivers will take 10-place grid penalties at Formula 1’s Brazilian Grand Prix for new internal combustion engines.

News of Lewis Hamilton’s grid penalty emerged earlier on Saturday, but it initially appeared Ferrari may wait for Las Vegas before team-mate Charles Leclerc took his new ICE, which would trigger a grid drop.
But confirmation came during third practice that both Hamilton and Leclerc would take a fifth ICE of the year in Brazil, automatically triggering a 10-place grid penalty.

Confirmation of Max Verstappen’s huge 30-place grid penalty also came as he’s taking a new ICE, exhaust, turbocharger and power unit ancillary component (within his allowance), which will mean he’ll start at the back of the grid regardless of where he qualifies.
Cadillac’s Sergio Perez will also take a new ICE, turbocharger and MGU-K - which will give him a 30-place grid penalty.
The Ferraris, Verstappen and Perez will join George Russell in taking grid penalties in Brazil.
Russell has a five-place grid penalty to serve, as he confirmed ahead of the weekend.
Russell - 5 places Leclerc, Hamilton - 10 places Perez, Verstappen - 30 places (back of the grid)

title: 5 Prestigious International Car Shows Where Automakers Reveal New Models
raw_summary: Changing industry dynamics and the rise of livestreaming have led many physical conventions and events to either go away entirely (most notably the Geneva Motor Show and the E3 video game expo) or shift to digital formats (Apple's major product keynotes). Thankfully, a lot of traditional car shows have stuck around globally and remain among the most important entries on the calendar for automakers. article_paragraphs: Changing industry dynamics and the rise of livestreaming have led many physical conventions and events to either go away entirely (most notably the Geneva Motor Show and the E3 video game expo) or shift to digital formats (Apple's major product keynotes). Thankfully, a lot of traditional car shows have stuck around globally and remain among the most important entries on the calendar for automakers.

Setting up a pavilion at an auto show, especially a reputable and longstanding one, can be expensive, but it gives automakers a global platform to unveil brand-new production cars, showcase wild concepts and designs , and introduce new technologies to journalists, industry executives, and prospective buyers. It's also always fun to walk through the pavilions at a motor show and check out new cars up close and in the flesh.

While hundreds of automotive exhibitions and trade shows are held across the world every year, there's an upper echelon of car shows for which automakers save their best reveals. These include long-running motor shows like IAA Mobility, exhibitions of growing significance like Auto China and Auto Shanghai, and Monterey Car Week, which isn't a convention but a week-long series of prestigious automotive events.

The Paris Motor Show, also known as Mondial de l'Auto, is one of the world's oldest automotive conventions, dating all the way back to 1898. Held biennially in the French capital, the Paris Motor Show has historically been a major platform for the country's top domestic automakers — Renault, Peugeot, Citroen, and the like — to reveal their latest and greatest to the world.

These include the Peugeot 402 in 1935 (one of the first European cars to feature a curvy, streamlined design), the Renault 4CV in 1946 and Citroen 2CV in 1948 (both instrumental in bringing personal mobility to a post-World War II, cash-strapped France), the Renault 5 Turbo in 1978 (a raucous 160-hp mid-engined supermini), and more. Landmark introductions from non-French automakers include the Lamborghini Sesto Elemento in 2010 and the Ferrari 250 Europa GT in 1954, along with the Porsche Carrera GT concept and Koenigsegg CC8S in 2000.

The 2026 iteration of the Paris Motor Show was held in October, and prominently featured concept cars like an all-electric revival of the Citroen 2CV , the striking Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso, the Peugeot E-T16 and RCZ Vision, the Alpine A310 Vision, the Renault E-Space, and the Fiat Multiplay.

Germany's International Motor Show or Internationale Automobil-Ausstellung, now branded IAA Mobility, beats the Paris Motor Show by just one year to claim the title of the oldest surviving car show in the world. Throughout its 129-year history, the biennial event has been held in various German cities, including Frankfurt am Main, Berlin, Leipzig, Cologne, and Munich. In a similar vein to the Paris Motor Show, IAA Mobility serves as a major showcase for Germany's big automakers, like BMW, Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, and Porsche.

Notable debuts at the IAA throughout history include the BMW 1500 in 1961 (it introduced the brand-saving Neue Klasse lineup), a concept version of the Volkswagen Golf GTI in 1975 (widely considered the forefather of hot hatchbacks), the Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.3-16 in 1983 (the record-breaking pioneer of sporty compact luxury sedans), the Audi RS6 Avant in 2007 (a super-cool V10-powered wagon), the Porsche 918 Spyder in 2013 (part of the holy trinity of hybrid hypercars), and many more.

raw_title: Lamborghini Gallardo’s Original Designer Polishes His Masterpiece
title: Lamborghini Gallardo's Original Designer Polishes His Masterpiece
raw_summary: Before it threw in the towel and decided to get in the luxury crossover game with the Urus, the Gallardo was Lamborghini's bestselling model. Careful input from parent company, Audi, meant a rip-roaring V-10 and all-wheel-drive grip, and Italian design house Italdesign clothed this in angular styling that merged supercar and stealth fighter into a great-looking machine. It wasn't the top-dog Lamborghini at the time, but it packed a punch. The initial work at Italdesign was done by none other than Fabrizio Giugiaro, son of the legendary Giorgetto. The Gallardo would later be polished by Luc Donckerwolke, but it seems like Fabrizio had a few finishing touches of his own to add. Thanks to Cavën Atelier, a Spanish engineering firm, Giugiaro Jr. has had a crack at reworking his 2003 original with modern tech and plenty of tweaks.

It wasn't the top-dog Lamborghini at the time, but it packed a punch.

The initial work at Italdesign was done by none other than Fabrizio Giugiaro, son of the legendary Giorgetto. The Gallardo would later be polished by Luc Donckerwolke, but it seems like Fabrizio had a few finishing touches of his own to add. Thanks to Cavën Atelier, a Spanish engineering firm, Giugiaro Jr. has had a crack at reworking his 2003 original with modern tech and plenty of tweaks.

The Hommage 26 starts with a donor Gallardo, similar to the Encor Series 1 Lotus Esprit restomod, which is then thoroughly reworked with carbon-fiber bodywork throughout. The front end resembles the original, but now incorporates modern lighting and pop-down headlights.

Like an old silhouette Trans-Am Audi, only the top sliver of the car is unchanged, with the same roofline and glass. Everything else is subtly reshaped, including a new rear fascia with massive rectangular exhaust pipes and integrated rear active aerodynamic panels like those you might find in a Pagani Huayra .

Under this new skin, the car's 5.0-liter V-10 now spins to 8500 rpm, producing either 533 hp in GT trim or as much as 552 in full-fat Performance spec. There’s active suspension, upgraded brakes, and the Hommage 26 rolls on 20-inch wheels.

Cost? The equivalent of a Dr. Evil-approved $1 million, plus you have to B.Y.O. Gallardo. That is an astounding amount of money for a restomod version of a non-V-12 Lamborghini, and it seems almost like a litmus test of just how much the restomod market boom will bear. Only 25 examples are planned to be built.

Perhaps more interestingly, Cavën Atelier positions the Hommage 26 not as a one-off, but as a potential series of cars that will see designers return to their work for upcoming reboots. The options here are endless: Ken Okuyama redoes the Ferrari Enzo ? A Camilo Pardo reworked first-generation Ford GT ? Even if the price tags will be out of reach, the designs will be interesting to see.

In the meantime, your standard Gallardo remains pretty accessible for how exotic it looks and drives. Put aside a little money for an Akrapovič exhaust, and enjoy it just as Giugiaro originally imagined.

raw_title: Is The 'Five-Year Rule' For Tires Still True?
title: Is The 'Five-Year Rule' For Tires Still True?
raw_summary: Tire age vs. tire mileage: here is the real truth behind the legendary five-year replacement rule. There's a popular saying that if your tires are over five years old, you should change them — even if the car they are mounted to doesn't drive that often. Today, it's pretty easy to check tire age: just look for the four-digit date code on the sidewall, and you'll know the week and year of manufacture.

article_paragraphs: Tire age vs. tire mileage: here is the real truth behind the legendary five-year replacement rule.

There's a popular saying that if your tires are over five years old, you should change them — even if the car they are mounted to doesn't drive that often. Today, it's pretty easy to check tire age: just look for the four-digit date code on the sidewall, and you'll know the week and year of manufacture.

However, the commonly quoted "five-year rule" was introduced decades back. Surely, tire tech has changed to allow for longer lifespans? The short answer is, the five-year rule may still hold in most cases, but even manufacturers are hesitant to cite it as a definitive cut-off. It turns out that, yes, there are situations where you might be able to stretch to six, seven years, or even more. However, after your tire crosses that five-year mark, you're best served keeping a vigilant eye on them.

Let's start with when you buy new tires. Just because they're new on the car doesn't mean they're newly made. When you're buying new rubber for your ride, you must select the freshest tires possible. This means that you should look for the ones that have been manufactured most recently. As a prime example, let's look at buying tires right now, in 2026. You'd do well to look at tires manufactured in the last three months — that's July through September. Going a bit further back is also okay, say, March or April.

But if you select a tire made in, say, late 2025, you've lost a year of life before it's even reached your hands. And remember, these are the tires that salespersons try to aggressively flog because they need to move them ASAP. It's not bad buying such a tire, but you should expect a discount when doing so.

If you're wondering what's so bad about aged tires, well, rubber ages with time. With that age comes the added risk of a potential blowout. As the rubber ages, in some cases tiny cracks can form that compromise the tire's integrity. These start on a microscopic level, but as time passes by, they become visible to the eye. If you see cracks on the sidewalls of your tires, it's time for a replacement, pronto, because one day, that tire is going to let go.

Tires do this due to how they're constructed and the materials they're made from. Tires are created by methods that include curing. These use compounds that age and break down over time due to thermo-oxidative degradation. Simply put, oxygen slowly breaks down the tire's rubber compound. But there are other factors that accelerate tire aging.

Tires also age faster in hot climates, so if you live in areas with plenty of sun and frequently drive on blisteringly hot tarmac, you should inspect your tires more often. But tires still age when sitting in a dark warehouse — just slower. The same applies to your spare tire, even if it's sitting cozy inside your vehicle's trunk. As for vehicles with exposed or underslung spare wheels that get exposed to sun, rain, dirt, and road grime, they need even more attention.

raw_title: We Tried Audi’s Revised Infotainment System to See If It’s Better
title: We Tried Audi's Revised Infotainment System to See If It's Better
raw_summary: Like many automakers, Audi is listening to the backlash towards touch-sensitive controls. It’s been implementing subtle changes to its infotainment interface and other controls to improve the user interface, and we recently got a chance to try these updates in a 2027 Audi Q6 e-tron . The Q6 e-tron (and its A6 e-tron sedan stablemate) launched for the 2025 model year. After skipping the 2026 model year, the 2027 model-year examples of these EVs underwent changes to the steering wheel to incorporate more physical controls and to the MMI infotainment software to simplify the interface. Similar changes have been propagating across the Audi lineup since. To start, there are new physical scroll wheels on the two steering-wheel spokes. The one on the left spoke controls the digital gauge cluster and cycles through different screens, while the one on the right spoke is a volume knob. There are still haptic buttons on the new wheel, but they’re responsive, and we prefer this setup to the previous one, which had only touch-sensitive buttons. The wheels are both simpler to use and have a satisfying click.

Audi also says it simplified the menu structures and changed the appearance of the display of its MMI infotainment interface, seen both on the central display screen and in the digital gauge cluster. We found the system easy to operate, with quick responses to inputs on the touchscreen, and the new appearance makes the built-in software look and feel a bit more like Apple CarPlay, with larger icons and simple backgrounds. Some of the vehicle-settings menus are still complex, but day-to-day functions such as audio controls and navigation were logical enough to use. As is the norm these days, over-the-air updates mean that Audi is also adding new functions to the system, such as the newly available Spotify app that allows you to access the streaming service in the car’s system without tethering it to your phone.

We’d still skip the optional passenger display screen, which seems unnecessary and is somewhat limited in its functions. Plus, given the amount of screen real estate already present on the dashboard, the addition of a third, 10.9-inch screen makes the entire dash look like a screen. The passenger display is available as part of the $1800 Technology package on the Premium Plus trim, and it comes standard in the top Prestige trim.

Despite being raised on a steady diet of base-model Hondas and Toyotas—or perhaps because of it—Joey Capparella cultivated an obsession for the automotive industry throughout his childhood in Nashville, Tennessee. He found a way to write about cars for the school newspaper during his college years at Rice University, which eventually led him to move to Ann Arbor, Michigan, for his first professional auto-writing gig at Automobile Magazine . He has been part of the Hearst Autos team since 2016 and now lives in New York City.

title: Are These 9 Concepts And Sporty Coupés Pre-Ford Mustang Pony Cars?
raw_summary: History books love romantic tales, like the one where Lee Iacocca, father of the Mustang, was responsible for giving birth to a whole new category of vehicles: pony cars. Sure, he was behind the creation of the most popular such vehicle, but the pony car concept was in the brewing stage years before the first-gen Mustang Mk1. article_paragraphs: History books love romantic tales, like the one where Lee Iacocca, father of the Mustang, was responsible for giving birth to a whole new category of vehicles: pony cars. Sure, he was behind the creation of the most popular such vehicle, but the pony car concept was in the brewing stage years before the first-gen Mustang Mk1. While not strictly pony cars, these concepts and production sporty coupés already flirted with the concept of an enthusiast-grade compact car.

Of course, we don't mean to diminish Iacocca's genius. Yes, he didn't invent the wheel, but he definitely read the room better than his counterparts. In fact, some of the cars featured in this piece influenced him to create the special team of engineers that worked on the Mustang. From early Ford-based compact sports cars like the Budd XT-Bird Concept and Ford Falcon Futura Sport to rear-engine fun machines like the Chevrolet Corvair Monza Turbo, these pre-Mustang models warmed the public to the pony car idea.

Iacocca wasn't the first to toy with the idea of a compact sports car for the masses. Edward Gowan Budd, one of the early 20th century's most important engineers and entrepreneurs, already had dabbled with the idea of a 2+2 sports car for the masses. Better yet, he pitched a working prototype of the XT-Bird directly to Iacocca, likely planting the pony-car seed in his mind.

The proposed car was based on a 1961 Ford Falcon unibody and a modified body shell from a 1955 to 1957 Ford Thunderbird. This let Budd's company, Budd-American Motors, stretch the Thunderbird's 102-inch wheelbase by 7.5 inches, turning it from a two-seater into a 2+2. Yes, the rear seats were tight and mostly unusable, but the 2+2 configuration became a hallmark of pony cars, allowing buyers to take their friends and family on a joyride.

Speaking of which, the XT-Bird Concept was equipped with a 170-cubic-inch (2.8-liter) inline-6 engine. Yes, it's not a V8, but Budd boosted it with a supercharger, so it should've been potent enough for the time. Power figures were never disclosed, but we know the XT-Bird Concept had a three-speed manual.

While the XT-Bird Concept influenced Ford in developing the Mustang, its clumsy attempt to modernize the classic Thunderbird fell flat. Budd smoothed out the Thunderbird's rear fins and accentuated headlight housings, resulting in a bland, somewhat forgettable design.

Ford never accepted Budd's XT-Bird proposal, but that didn't stop the ambitious engineer from making another attempt at an early pony car. Unveiled mere months later, the XR-400 Concept was another fully functional, production-ready sporty convertible.

This time, though, Budd used a Rambler Ambassador chassis and proposed the idea to American Motors Corporation. He went so far to create a full development plan, estimating a low $4.1 million to bring the car to market. Because the XR-400 Concept utilized an existing AMC platform, tooling and production would've also been cheaper than building the car from the ground up. Had AMC greenlit the XR-400, it would've beaten both the Barracuda and the Mustang to showroom floors, completely rewriting pony car history. Heck, it might even have saved AMC from the Chrysler buyout. Instead, AMC surrendered its head start and played catch-up with the other old-school pony cars using the 1968 Javelin.

article_paragraphs: I had the pleasure of experiencing Buc-ee's Beaver Nuggets for the first time on a recent road trip. It's an experience I'll get to repeat soon as the popular chain of ginormous gas stations and convenience stores expands into my adopted home state of Arkansas, among other places . It'll be interesting to see if the midterm election results affect those expansion plans, as Buc-ee's president and co-founder Arch "Beaver" Aplin III has expressed a desire to avoid blue states, according to Fox Business .
At the grand opening of a new location in Benton, Arkansas, Aplin said:

"I'm starting to realize life's too short to try to build in places that people don't appreciate what you're bringing, versus a place like this where people do appreciate what you are building," he said.
Conservative states typically promote business-friendly and family-oriented policies that align with Buc-ee's values, Aplin said.

"That leadership, that concept, that idea of conservative, business-friendly, family-oriented concept works so much better if it trickles down from the very leadership from the top at the governor's office, at the congressman, at senator, at the mayor, the representatives," he said.

The thing is, Aplin no longer has that choice. The blue tsunami of the midterm election has turned several states formerly controlled by Republicans over to the Democrats at many of those levels, and in some cases all of them.

The most notable upset from the election is right in Buc-ee's home state of Texas. President Trump hand-picked the scandal-ridden Ken Paxton to run against Democratic contender James Talarico for U.S. Senate, pushing out incumbent Republican John Cornyn during the primaries (maybe he won't be able to steal the Space Shuttle after all). Elon Musk invested more than $200 million backing Paxton's election campaign. Despite all that, Talarico won, making him the first Democratic Senator from Texas since 1993. Ted Cruz remains in the Senate, but possibly only because he wasn't up for re-election this year.

It's not just the Senate, either. Governor Greg Abbott lost re-election to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, and the Texas House gained a slight Democratic majority as well. Buc-ee's now finds itself deeply entrenched and headquartered in a blue state, as unlikely as it was for Texas to flip like this. If Buc-ee's really doesn't want to do business in blue states, it's going to have to find a new home. So will Elon Musk , for that matter, just five years after fleeing California for the same reason.

article_paragraphs: Two-wheeler retail sales in India witnessed a significant year-on-year (YoY) decline in October 2026, with total registrations falling to 23,21,419 units. According to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA), the overall automotive retail market also registered a sharp decline, primarily due to a shift in the festive calendar.

While Navratri fell in October this year, Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations have moved to November, impacting vehicle purchases during the month. Despite this sharp YoY decline, FADA noted that October 2026 was the second-best October on record for two-wheeler retail sales.

Petrol/ethanol-powered two-wheelers continued to dominate the Indian market, accounting for 90.30% of total retail sales in October 2026. Electric two-wheelers contributed a 9.65% share, while CNG/LPG-powered models accounted for the remaining 0.05%.

Demand trends indicated stronger sales momentum in urban markets as compared to that seen in rural areas. Rural demand was impacted due to deficient rainfall, coupled with a weak Kharif crop which had an adverse effect on consumer sentiment and purchasing activity.

Total two-wheeler retail sales stood at 23,21,419 units in October 2026, down 28.35% from 32,39,949 units registered in October 2025. However, on a month-on-month (MoM) basis, sales improved by 29.67% compared to 17,90,188 units recorded in September 2026 .

On a year-to-date (YTD) basis, covering April to October 2026, two-wheeler retail sales reached 1,33,79,362 units. This represented a 7.81% increase over the 1,24,09,794 units registered during the corresponding period last year.

Honda once again commanded the sales list with 6,37,630 unit sales with a strong 27.47% market share. Hero MotoCorp sales declined sharply on a YoY basis to 5,98,433 units from 10,06,796 units of Oct 2025 bringing down its market share to 25.78%.

TVS Motor sales also dipped to 4,58,303 units YoY though market share improved to 19.74%. Combined sales of Honda, Hero and TVS, which stood at 16,94,366 units, accounted for more than 72% of two-wheeler retail market during the month of October 2026.

title: Iridium Vs. Platinum Spark Plugs: Are There Performance Or Efficiency Differences?
raw_summary: If you know anything about internal combustion, you'll know that spark plugs are key to performance and efficiency. But there are two main types of spark plugs on offer today: iridium and platinum, and the choice of spark plug can make a difference on how your car engine performs. That said, it's more nuanced than simply choosing one over the other, and it greatly depends on the application. First, the basics. Spark plugs in a gasoline engine play a key role because, without them, the gas-air mixture would not combust, and simply put, you'd go nowhere. But even though they're a cornerstone of any gas engine — virtually as old as the invention itself — the tech behind them continues to develop. In the old days, spark plugs were made of copper. Copper is no longer used on modern cars because it wears out relatively quickly inside a cylinder of exploding gas that can routinely exceed 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit in normal operation. So, which type of spark plug is better? To answer that, we need to discuss which is most cost-effective for your situation and whether can you mix and match the two.
summary: If you know anything about internal combustion, you'll know that spark plugs are key to performance and efficiency. But there are two main types of spark plugs on offer today: iridium and platinum, and the choice of spark plug can make a difference on how your car engine performs.
article_paragraphs: If you know anything about internal combustion, you'll know that spark plugs are key to performance and efficiency. But there are two main types of spark plugs on offer today: iridium and platinum, and the choice of spark plug can make a difference on how your car engine performs. That said, it's more nuanced than simply choosing one over the other, and it greatly depends on the application. First, the basics. Spark plugs in a gasoline engine play a key role because, without them, the gas-air mixture would not combust, and simply put, you'd go nowhere.

But even though they're a cornerstone of any gas engine — virtually as old as the invention itself — the tech behind them continues to develop. In the old days, spark plugs were made of copper. Copper is no longer used on modern cars because it wears out relatively quickly inside a cylinder of exploding gas that can routinely exceed 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit in normal operation. So, which type of spark plug is better? To answer that, we need to discuss which is most cost-effective for your situation and whether can you mix and match the two.

Whether or not you go for platinum or iridium spark plugs is highly dependent on your car and its engine. With a melting point of over 3,200 degrees Fahrenheit, platinum is perfect for most daily driving applications. It's tough, durable, and cost-effective, with platinum spark plugs capable of lasting beyond 60,000 miles in a well-maintained engine. Iridium plugs, on the other hand, are your high-performance heroes.

If you've got a powerful vehicle with a high-performance engine — one that's turbocharged and/or high-revving — it almost definitely needs iridium plugs. In fact, many modern engines come from the factory with iridium spark plugs in a quest for more efficiency and durability. Iridium spark plugs have a melting point of around 4,400 degrees Fahrenheit, meaning they can handle the increased temperatures of highly-strung gasoline powerplants. Plus, they come with ultra-fine electrodes that generate a more precise and cleaner spark.

This has a double benefit; in addition to optimal power, it also provides better fuel efficiency. So, what is the main disadvantage of iridium spark plugs? Iridium spark plugs can be expensive compared to their platinum counterparts — although probably not as pricey as quoted by one Dodge dealership. In fact, they can cost over twice as much as an equivalent platinum spark plug. But, if you've got a performance car that requires this type of spark plug, then yes, they are worth the extra money.

Now that you know about platinum and iridium spark plugs, you should have a better idea about how they affect your car's performance and efficiency. But when it comes to mixing the two, it's a pretty hard no. You shouldn't do this under any circumstances. Using a mix of iridium and platinum plugs in your engine will cause myriad issues, since combustion won't be well-matched across all cylinders. If you're replacing the spark plugs, you need to replace all of them with the correct type, at the same time.

As well, you won't get a performance boost if you install iridium plugs in an engine designed for platinum plugs, even when it's a $20,000 job on a Bugatti. You'll only be draining your wallet unnecessarily. By the same token, if you think you can install platinum plugs in an engine designed for iridium, you shouldn't do this either, as there will be issues with performance and fuel efficiency. At the end of the day, the best advice we can give you is to consult what the manufacturer has specified and stick to that, whether that be platinum or iridium spark plugs.

title: Harbinger scores another $240M in latest investment round
raw_summary: Electric truck maker Harbinger has been racking up wins in recent months, and after scoring a $300 million order from international shipping giant FedEx and a defense contract with the US military, the company has drummed up another $240 million in Series D funding. Companies like FedEx and Amazon have been making serious moves to fully electrify their fleet operations, both in an effort to decarbonize and to avoid the every-increasing price of diesel . At $300 million for 2,000 medium-duty electric delivery trucks, Harbinger’s latest deal with FedEx is believed to be one of the largest binding orders for electric medium or heavy-duty trucks in history – and it’s a big enough deal to inspire more than 240 million votes of confidence in the company’s future, one dollar at a time.

“Harbinger exists to challenge what industry has learned to accept, and reinvent the critical systems the world depends on,” said John Harris, the Co-Founder and CEO of Harbinger . “By rethinking critical systems from first principles, we aim to unlock better performance, greater reliability, safer operations, and more room to grow. Electrification is at the core of everything we do, and increasingly, electrification is at the core of industry, defense, mobility, and AI. Harbinger’s role is not simply to give customers another option. It is to reset expectations for what critical systems should deliver.”

Harbinger’s Series D funding round was co-led by Tiger Global, the Capricorn Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. The company says the new funding will support expansion into energy storage systems, power generation, autonomy software, and defense applications , as well as the continued ramp up of its medium-duty platform manufacturing capacity. With this latest round of financing, Harbinger has raised over $650 million since 2021.
As for me, I’m hoping they use the money to come up with more fun, high-octane chase videos that show off their trucks’ performance capabilities . Time will tell.

That’s an important distinction in European cities, where larger wheels can make quick work of the cobblestones, potholes, and tram tracks that can turn smaller-wheeled scooters into teeth-rattling experiences.

The XENTER E uses Yamaha’s new eAxle powertrain, combining the motor, controller, and reduction gearbox into a compact frame-mounted unit. The motor produces 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power and 33.3 Nm of torque, putting the scooter into Europe’s A1 license category.

Mounting the motor to the frame also means Yamaha can use a more conventional motorcycle-style swingarm rather than hanging the motor on the rear suspension like many scooters. That reduces unsprung weight and should help improve handling and ride quality.

Power is supplied from an integrated 3.5 kWh battery mounted low in the chassis. Yamaha claims 108 km (67 miles) of range on the WMTC Class 1 cycle, though real-world range is expected to be somewhat lower.
An 800W onboard charger can refill the battery in around 5.5 hours from a public charging station. Yamaha will also offer a cable for charging from a household outlet.

Other niceties include three riding modes, traction control, regenerative braking, a reverse mode for maneuvering at low speeds, smart-key operation, and a 5-inch TFT display. Smartphone connectivity adds navigation, battery information, maintenance reminders, and parking-location tracking.

While some automakers have abandoned the compact and midsize truck segments, the ones still going strong are pretty impressive. In particular, the Ford Maverick is nearly the perfect truck , even with its un-trucklike unibody design. And if its excellent hybrid fuel efficiency, spiffy handling, user-friendly tech, and agreeable ride don't sell it for you, then maybe some of its hidden features will.

You see, the 2027 Ford Maverick isn't exactly a what-you-see-is-what-you-get truck. The Maverick comes with standard and optional features that don't announce themselves with much fanfare but are highly useful when you know where to look and how to take advantage of them. Knowing how to access and use extra storage, onboard power, and a plethora of customizable safety features will take your Maverick ownership to the next level.

Yes, most pickups are designed for hauling, so lots of storage is to be expected. That's what the whole bed is for, even if the average truck owner doesn't actually use it for truck stuff. The Maverick goes above and beyond, though, in offering flexible and functional options, plus plentiful hidden storage. This should partially make up for the fact that its 54.4-inch bed is about a foot shorter than the smallest bed on an F-150.

When futzing with storage options in the bed, you'll find that the Maverick uses Ford's Flexbed design. This includes a multi-position tailgate and fixed tie-down points, two of which — found on the gate — double as bottle openers for when you're having a tailgate party or need a crisp pre-drive Topo Chico. A cargo management system with bed rails and a small cubby recessed into the body of the truck is also available, with a removable tray to unlock more space. There's even a QR code in the bed that links to ideas for exploring bed storage techniques. You can also option in-bed LED box lighting to keep the area illuminated while you're working in low light. Additionally, the bed has a grooved design intended to make it easy to build and install your own storage solutions using 2x4s or 2x6s.

In the cab itself, you'll find storage under the rear bench. It's big enough for a small backpack, camera gear, work boots, or whatever tickles your fancy. Door storage gives enough room for decently sized water bottles, and there's additional storage space behind the 13.2-inch infotainment screen. Of course, you'll find storage in the center console armrest, too.

It's not exactly a secret that you can option even the base XL trim with Co-Pilot360, a suite of safety and driver-assistance features. However, using the system to its fullest potential takes a little massaging, and you'll likely want to customize the system to your preferences for the best possible experience. After all, aren't customizability and adaptability the true meaning of truck ownership ?

Depending on the trim and options, a Maverick's version of Co-Pilot360 can include pre-collision assist with automatic emergency braking, a rearview camera, blind-spot monitoring with cross-traffic alert, lane-keep assist, automatic high-beam headlights, stop-and-go adaptive cruise control with lane centering, evasive steering assist, and post-collision braking. Co-Pilot360 technology also covers towing aids like Pro Trailer Hitch Assist. However, not every driver will want to have all of these features active all the time, and knowing how to turn certain features on or off piecemeal will lead to a better experience overall.

raw_summary: Honda makes just about everything with a motor, from lawnmowers and generators to cars, motorcycles, and even airplanes. Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the new Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market. And unlike many automotive-branded e-bikes that amount to little more than a licensing deal and a familiar logo slapped on someone else’s frame, Honda appears to have actually put some engineering muscle behind this one.

Now the Japanese giant is adding another electrified vehicle to the list – a premium electric mountain bike. Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the new Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market.
article_paragraphs: Honda makes just about everything with a motor, from lawnmowers and generators to cars, motorcycles, and even airplanes. Now the Japanese giant is adding another electrified vehicle to the list – a premium electric mountain bike.

Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the new Honda RN0 marks the company’s first entry into the premium electric mountain bike market. And unlike many automotive-branded e-bikes that amount to little more than a licensing deal and a familiar logo slapped on someone else’s frame, Honda appears to have actually put some engineering muscle behind this one.

The RN0 was jointly developed with German high-end e-MTB manufacturer ROTWILD and features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and distinctive gull-arm swingarm inspired by Honda’s motorcycle chassis development experience.

There’s actually some real history behind that connection. Honda experimented with mountain bike development in the early 2000s, culminating in its wild RN01 downhill racing bike. In 2005, that project won the overall series championship in the UCI Mountain Bike Downhill World Cup. Honda never turned the RN01 into a consumer bicycle, but more than two decades later, the RN0 is effectively picking up where the company previously left off.

The roughly 24 kg (53 lb) RN0 is set up as a multi-role electric mountain bike, featuring 160 mm FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima front suspension paired with a FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima rear shock. DT Swiss H1900 SPLINE wheels use a mullet setup with a 29-inch wheel up front and 27.5-inch wheel in the rear, while Shimano DEORE XT four-piston brakes handle stopping duties.
Those are some quality components, but the drivetrain may be even more interesting.
Honda is using Shimano’s new 2.3 kg drive unit, rated for up to 100 Nm of torque and 750 watts of maximum output, paired with a sizeable 720 Wh battery.
Shimano’s AUTO ASSIST can automatically vary motor assistance based on terrain and rider input, while AUTO SHIFT handles gear changes to maintain an appropriate cadence.

title: Gary Anderson's verdict on McLaren's 2027-leaning upgrade
raw_summary: No team wants to show its dirty washing in public, so McLaren calling its new front wing effectively a 2027 concept seems strange. In that position, assuming the numbers on track and the simulation tools show it has potential, I’d be using it now and considering it very much a 2026 part. article_paragraphs: No team wants to show its dirty washing in public, so McLaren calling its new front wing effectively a 2027 concept seems strange.

In that position, assuming the numbers on track and the simulation tools show it has potential, I’d be using it now and considering it very much a 2026 part. With (perhaps) four races remaining and roughly five months before the start of next season, I’d be learning as much as possible from it and would hopefully make a step or two as a result of it before next season kicks off.
The intersection between the mainplane and the lower foot of the endplate, highlighted with the red ellipse, is what caught my eye.

Red Bull started the season with this concept, and Mercedes and others have followed. Making it more of a single lower surface reduces the sensitivity of the endplate footplate to the track, so in high-speed corners the front of the car should produce more consistent downforce. Basically, it should feel less snatchy, making the rear of the car more stable.
The slot gap profile between the forward and central elements, highlighted with the green arrow, has also been altered.

This is in line with the profile change highlighted with the light blue arrow and the positioning of the longest chord section of the third element. With that section slightly more inboard, this will alter where the mass flow reaches the leading edge of the floor.

What confuses me a little is the change from reducing the angle of the second and third elements in straight mode to reducing only the angle of the third when straight mode is activated. It means that the front wing is less powerful in corner mode, but that comes at the expense of overall downforce.

When the wing is in cornering mode (max downforce), the low pressure on the lower surface will pull more of its airflow through the slot gap between the first and second elements. To compensate for this, McLaren has reduced the chord length of the mainplane, highlighted with the green arrow, and increased the chord length of the second element, highlighted with the light blue arrow.

title: Diesel Pickups Get Better MPGs Than Gas, But Is It Enough To Counteract Diesel Prices?
raw_summary: For this piece, we're placing ourselves into the shoes of a pickup truck buyer who wants to get the best value-for-money deal possible from a new truck. Fuel prices remain near record highs, even after Trump's dirty Russian oil deal , so it's reasonable to expect buyers to make fuel costs a major deciding factor when looking at which truck to take home. In fact, as of this writing, the latest EIA figures see gas at $4.28 per gallon, while diesel sits at $6.27. On the face of it then, it would appear that gas is the way to go, but the math isn't that straightforward. Diesel trucks are more efficient per gallon, as a general rule, so that gallon will return more miles, in theory. If it returns sufficient additional miles, it then becomes the more cost-effective fuel, despite setting owners back more at the pump.

article_paragraphs: For this piece, we're placing ourselves into the shoes of a pickup truck buyer who wants to get the best value-for-money deal possible from a new truck. Fuel prices remain near record highs, even after Trump's dirty Russian oil deal , so it's reasonable to expect buyers to make fuel costs a major deciding factor when looking at which truck to take home.

In fact, as of this writing, the latest EIA figures see gas at $4.28 per gallon, while diesel sits at $6.27. On the face of it then, it would appear that gas is the way to go, but the math isn't that straightforward. Diesel trucks are more efficient per gallon, as a general rule, so that gallon will return more miles, in theory. If it returns sufficient additional miles, it then becomes the more cost-effective fuel, despite setting owners back more at the pump.

Now, heavy-duty trucks are exempt from standard EPA fuel economy testing, which makes picking between gas and diesel a little trickier. Thankfully, Car and Driver has been testing such trucks on a 200-mile fuel-efficiency highway route for the last 10 years, so we can use its data to determine whether diesel- or gas-powered trucks work out to be the more cost-effective choice.

As it happens, the outlet's 2024 roundup highlighted that diesel trucks on average return 18 mpg, while gas trucks net 15, so there's a 20% increase in fuel efficiency when running on diesel. Sounds great, but using the aforementioned figures, diesel is 46.5% more expensive, so a thirsty gas-guzzling truck is still kinder on the pocket.

Of course, those are only generalized figures taken from across all models tested. The outlet has run a total of 22 heavy-duty models on its 200-mile efficiency route. Of those, the top five most efficient models were all diesel-powered, and the top two managed to eke out 20 mpg. They are the 2018 Ram 2500 Limited Crew Cab, and the 2023 Ford F-250 Super Duty Platinum Tremor Crew Cab, powered respectively by standard-output Cummins and high-output Power Stroke engines.

Putting a Cummins against a Power Stroke engine highlights pros and cons for each camp, but regardless of which each individual favors, it's hard to argue with how impressive 20 mpg is, considering the size and heft of the trucks they each power. Still, that extra 2 mpg sadly doesn't make the difference when it comes to cost-per-mile, although it does help to close the gap significantly.

Using the above per-gallon prices, a 20-mpg diesel truck still costs around 10% more than a 15-mpg gas truck, costing $0.31 each mile, against the gas truck's $0.29. For the math to swing into the diesel truck's favor, it would have to be returning at least 22 mpg, at which point, it would cost almost exactly the same per mile as the gas truck.

We aren't about to suggest you start employing hypermiling techniques to get a few extra miles out of an old Cummins-powered Ram, like overinflating the tires, or stripping weight out by throwing air-conditioning units and back seats away. However, there are some useful tips you can follow to get better fuel economy .

title: New Maruti Electric MPV To Be Unveiled In February 2027
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Maruti Suzuki to launch its first pure electric people mover in quick succession after the e Vitara, challenging the Kia Carens Clavis EV Not long after introducing the e Vitara, Maruti Suzuki has started development of its second electric car, which will be an MPV. The company is likely to unveil it at the biennial Auto Expo, set to be held in February 2027. During Maruti Suzuki’s Q2 FY2027 earnings conference call, Chief Investor Relations Officer Rahul Bharti revealed that the company plans to launch its next EV at Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027. In all likelihood, he was referring to the aforementioned electric MPV Codenamed ‘Maruti YMC’, the electric MPV is being tested on public roads since summer this year. Recently, Instagram user carlord_767 spotted one of the several prototypes of the Maruti YMC undergoing tests on the road. A spy video shared by the spotter has shown several details of the model’s exterior. At the rear, we can see the Maruti YMC featuring Maruti Ertiga-like vertical LED tail lights. The tail lights are connected via a horizontal strip, although we doubt it is illuminated. An LED high-mounted stop lamp and a shark-fin antenna can also be seen. Also Read: Huge Diwali Discounts On Maruti Suzuki Arena Cars; Up To Rs. 1.21 Lakh Image Source: CarIndiaNews The side profile has a boxy appearance but leans more toward SUV than MPV. The beltline is set quite high, leading to a sleek look for the greenhouse. These attributes, as well as the angular, squared-off wheel arches, make the Maruti YMC reminiscent of the Maruti e Vitara from the sides. 18-inch alloy wheels will likely be part of the standard equipment. Previous sightings have indicated that the front end of the Maruti YMC will likely also have hints of the Maruti e Vitara. Here, too, the car will look more SUV than an MPV. The bonnet should be set high and have a largely flattish design. The headlamps should be horizontal but have vertical extensions. The nose section is likely to be covered with a body-coloured surface. Also Read: Maruti Suzuki Records 2.76 Lakh Units In October 2026, Sales Rise 25% Image Source: Harsh Vlogs/Youtube Maruti Suzuki will likely offer the YMC in seven- and six-seat versions, with the latter featuring captain’s chairs in the second row. We expect two power-electric variants, both with a single motor powering the front wheels. The base variant’s motor should produce 105.8 kW (142 hp) and 193 Nm of torque, and the top variant’s motor will likely develop 128 kW (172 hp) and 193 Nm of torque. The former will likely draw power from a 48.8 kWh LFP battery pack, and the latter should draw power from a 61.1 kWh LFP unit. We expect the top variant to have a range of approximately 525 kilometres.

raw_title: Mahindra BE 7 Spied In BKC Mumbai – With GNSS Receiver On Roof
title: Mahindra BE 7 Spied In BKC Mumbai
raw_summary: Mahindra Auto has been testing and developing BE 7 for some time now and there have been multiple spy shots of it. Latest ones show BE 7 from close proximity and in much greater detail than before. Also, we can see some additional antenna equipment retrofitted on top of the roof which will probably not make it to production. These added antenna equipment look like they are high precision receivers for Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and they help locate the vehicle accurately down to a centimeter. These latest spy shots of Mahindra BE 7 test mule with GNSS receiver were captured in BKC area of Mumbai, India.

article_paragraphs: Mahindra Auto has been testing and developing BE 7 for some time now and there have been multiple spy shots of it. Latest ones show BE 7 from close proximity and in much greater detail than before. Also, we can see some additional antenna equipment retrofitted on top of the roof which will probably not make it to production.

These added antenna equipment look like they are high precision receivers for Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and they help locate the vehicle accurately down to a centimeter. These latest spy shots of Mahindra BE 7 test mule with GNSS receiver were captured in BKC area of Mumbai, India.

There are two XEVs in the portfolio (XEV 9e, XEV 9S), but only one BE offering (BE 6), which will change soon with BE 7. The launch timeline is not known yet and 2027 could be the year. There have been multiple test mule sightings up until now and the latest spy shots show BE 7 test mules with GNSS receivers on top.

Currently, there are two fully operational GNSS systems – GPS from USA and GLONASS from Russia. There are other regional systems as well, including the recently operational India’s NavIC system. GNSS systems include constellations of satellites orbiting earth, broadcasting locations across space and time.

These broadcasted locations across ground control stations are crucial to calculate ground positions. GNSS systems are beneficial across a wide range of transportation from space travel and aviation to mass transportation too. Presence of these GNSS antennas on Mahindra BE 7 test mule could suggest multiple things including a next gen in-built navigation or even location-based ADAS features.

The latest spy shots of Mahindra BE 7 are snagged from BKC area in Mumbai, by Reddit user DemorganX. We can see full camouflage on this test mule and then Mahindra’s new flush door handles that are fully automated like in a Tesla or BYD. It will be India’s first mainstream vehicle to get frameless windows too, which buyers are likely to appreciate (I certainly would).

We can see the new clamshell bonnet along with large C-shaped lighting elements. Large wheels (presumably 19-inchers), angular wheel arch claddings and hidden rear washer and wiper are notable. Charging flap is on the rear left quarter panel, where one would usually see a fuel filler cap. BE 7 is a much larger vehicle and has a more SUV-like silhouette, when compared to BE 6.

On the inside, Mahindra BE 7 dashboard is expected to be closer to its concept form without a halo loop around driver. Centre console and sporty seats might be similar to that of BE 6’s. A triple screen dashboard can be seen in these spy shots too and other expected attributes are ventilated seats, 1400W 16 speaker Harman system, Adrenox suite, Level-2+ ADAS, powered seats, fancy ambient lighting, auto parking features and more.

title: Car Retail Sales Oct 2026 - Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai, Kia, Toyota, Skoda VW, MG, Honda
raw_summary: India’s passenger vehicle retail sales stood at 5,07,768 units in October 2026, registering a 14.23% year-on-year (YoY) decline compared to 5,92,032 units sold in October 2025. However, sales recorded a strong month-on-month (MoM) growth of 18.86% over the 4,27,213 units retailed in September 2026 . This YoY decline can largely be attributed to a shift in the festive calendar, with key occasions such as Dhanteras and Diwali falling in November this year. Dhanteras will be celebrated on November 6, followed by Diwali on November 8, 2026, pushing a significant portion of festive vehicle purchases into the following month. However, despite the annual decline, October 2026 recorded the third-highest October retail sales in history, highlighting the underlying strength of this segment.

However, sales recorded a strong month-on-month (MoM) growth of 18.86% over the 4,27,213 units retailed in September 2026 .

This YoY decline can largely be attributed to a shift in the festive calendar, with key occasions such as Dhanteras and Diwali falling in November this year. Dhanteras will be celebrated on November 6, followed by Diwali on November 8, 2026, pushing a significant portion of festive vehicle purchases into the following month. However, despite the annual decline, October 2026 recorded the third-highest October retail sales in history, highlighting the underlying strength of this segment.

Cumulative retail sales for the period April-October 2026 period also remained encouraging. YTD sales increased by 16.14% to 30,68,353 units, up from 26,35,837 units retailed during the corresponding period last year.

In a fuel wise breakup, petrol/ethanol cars dominated with a 41.60% share while diesel held a 16.57% share and CNG/LPG commanded a 24.59% share. There was a significant rise in hybrid (strong + mild) and EVs which improved their market shares to 9.94% and 7.38% respectively. Urban and rural demand ended on a positive note with a 20.10% and 16.90% growth.

Maruti Suzuki continued to dominate the passenger vehicle retail market, registering sales of 2,11,996 units in October 2026 and commanding a market share of 41.75%. Tata Motors secured a No. 2 position with 73,449 units, overtaking Mahindra, which recorded sales of 64,982 units.

Tata Motors maintained an advantage of 8,467 units over Mahindra during the past month. However, both automakers strengthened their market positions, with market shares of 14.47% and 12.80%, respectively.

Hyundai Motor at No. 4 suffered a sales setback to 58,099 units in Oct 2026 from 69,458 units sold in Oct 2025 while Kia India overtook Toyota with 30,799 unit sales. Toyota sales dipped to 28,727 units from 38,367 units on a YoY basis taking down market share to 6%.

VW Skoda Group, which saw retail sales at 9,150 units in the past month, suffered a sequential decline in its market share to 1.80% from 2.27% held in the same month last year when sales had stood at 13,459 units.

raw_title: Mahindra Confirms 5 New Vehicle Launches In H1 2027 – Key Details
title: Mahindra Confirms 5 New Vehicle Launches In H1 2027
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The five launches comprise a NU_IQ model, an INGLO electric SUV, the Scorpio Lifestyler, a significant model revision and a new light commercial vehicle Mahindra has confirmed five new model launches for the first half of 2027 as the manufacturer prepares to introduce new SUVs and commercial vehicles. Rajesh Jejurikar, Executive Director and CEO of the Auto and Farm Sectors, outlined the plans at the Q2 FY27 media briefing. The schedule consists of the first production model on the NU_IQ architecture, an entirely new INGLO electric vehicle and the Scorpio Lifestyler pickup. A substantial revision to an existing vehicle and a new light commercial vehicle are also scheduled before the end of June 2027. The Scorpio Lifestyler is the only new passenger vehicle among these five whose production identity has been officially confirmed. Mahindra unveiled the pickup this past August and announced a launch by April 2027. Prices will start below Rs. 19.79 lakh (ex-showroom). Jejurikar also confirmed that the Lifestyler will be registered as a personal vehicle using a white number plate. Its upright front fascia, separate cargo bed and Scorpio styling distinguish it from the regular Scorpio N and it will be powered by a diesel mill. The first NU_IQ production vehicle could be derived from the Vision S concept unveiled in August 2025. Test vehicles believed to be based on the concept have been spotted repeatedly on Indian roads. The prototypes feature a boxy body, short overhangs, flush door handles and an externally mounted spare wheel. A panoramic sunroof has also been spotted and we expect the production Vision S to sit between XUV 3XO and Scorpio N. The NU_IQ monocoque architecture supports petrol, diesel, hybrid and electric powertrains. The second new vehicle will use the dedicated INGLO electric architecture. The BE 07 is a possible candidate as prototypes believed to belong to the model have already undergone road testing. Earlier images revealed a cabin featuring three dashboard screens and a large central console and it will design will be heavily influenced by the concept as well. The SUV could share the 59 kWh and 79 kWh battery options available on existing INGLO vehicles such as the BE 6. The significant model revision is another interesting part of the announcement as Mahindra already introduced updates for the Scorpio N and the Thar OG in 2026. The Thar Roxx is one possibility after recent test sightings indicated changes to the suspension and alloy wheels. However, Mahindra has not connected those prototypes to its 2027 product calendar. The fifth launch will be a new light commercial vehicle and the company recently introduced an updated Veero. Pic Source: Reddit – u/ParticularNext1196 Mahindra is also increasing production capacity at its Chakan manufacturing facility ahead of these introductions. Jejurikar confirmed that the company expects to establish approximately 8,000 units of additional monthly NU_IQ capacity by February or March 2027. Electric vehicle manufacturing capacity will rise by another 4,000 units per month to 12,000 units. The company has also acquired the initial parcel of land for its Nagpur manufacturing project and has begun execution work at the site. The new manufacturing investments come after Mahindra reported sales of around 1.83 lakh SUVs in the July to September 2026 quarter.

raw_title: BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme Shatters 500 Kmph Top Speed Barrier – World’s First
title: BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme Shatters 500 Kmph Top Speed Barrier - World's First
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The electric hypercar records 503.17 kmph on a closed Abu Dhabi highway securing FIA recognition and two Guinness World Records BYD had already established a 496.22 kmph speed record for the Yangwang U9 Xtreme in Germany in September 2025 but the electric hypercar has now crossed the 500 kmph barrier. Racing driver Marc Basseng clocked 503.17 kmph on a closed road in Abu Dhabi on November 1, 2026. The result made the U9 Xtreme the first production car to achieve the figure. The FIA recognised the run which surpassed the earlier attempt by 6.95 kmph. Guinness World Records certified two categories for the achievement: the highest one-way speed by a production car and the corresponding record for an electric production car. The measurement was independently verified using a calibrated VBOX system. An FIA official examined the data and confirmed the result. However, the attempt did not establish a two-way average which is required under other production car speed record protocols. The attempt took place on Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed International Road in the Al Dhafra region of Abu Dhabi. Local authorities closed a 10 km section of the E11 highway and a 7 km uninterrupted straight was available for the high speed runs. The road was swept before the attempts and engineers inspected the surface for small wire fragments left by road-sweeping brushes. Basseng had previously driven the same hypercar at Germany’s ATP Papenburg proving ground. The first two attempts on October 31 produced a maximum speed of 490 kmph. Engineers subsequently increased the rear wing angle to improve rear axle downforce, revised the suspension rebound calibration and adjusted tyre pressures. Battery and motor temperatures also received extra attention before the November 1 runs. The first attempt that day confirmed improvements in stability and tyre performance, and the second recorded the final 503.17 kmph figure. The U9 Xtreme uses four independent electric motors rated at 555 kW each. Their combined output stands at 3,019 PS. Each motor can operate at speeds of up to 30,000 rpm. The hypercar also uses a 1,200 V electrical architecture instead of the 800 V system found in the standard U9. Its lithium iron phosphate Blade Battery supports extremely high discharge rates while the e4 torque vectoring system adjusts power independently at each wheel more than 100 times per second. The active suspension is another essential component of the U9 Xtreme. Its DiSus-X system can generate up to 50 kN of vertical force in 120 milliseconds to control body movement. Giti developed specialised semi-slick tyres that use a dedicated compound and a treatment at the tyre rim interface to resist slippage under heavy acceleration or braking. Visually, the car features a low wedge-shaped nose, narrow lighting elements, a front splitter, an adjustable rear wing and a substantial rear diffuser. The U9 Xtreme has also completed the Nürburgring Nordschleife in 6 minutes 59.157 seconds. The car used the same technical specification as the record-breaking example. BYD plans to manufacture only 30 units worldwide. A production standard vehicle named Dawn Moment was displayed at the Beijing Auto Show earlier this year and some customers have already approved their individual specifications. The manufacturer is now progressing towards contract signing and production scheduling for those vehicles.
